tickets.title: Records stage 2: projections and eta in the kernel
tickets.body:
Kernel projections and eta, so `p = (p.fst, p.snd)` holds by `rfl` for pairs and records (docs/aoc-2025.md:1302-1303, 'No pair eta'); see docs/proposals/records.md draft 2 §7 (Stage 2: projections and eta in the kernel). Includes the same-type rule and eta off in unification's `first_order` fallback. Do after proof irrelevance (SW-93) is decided.

D8 (Matt, 19 Oct): not now; build when proofs about records need it.

History: this was the 'Records follow-ups' umbrella. Split 19 Oct into SW-119 (done), SW-120 (termination through record fields, backlog), SW-121 (done); (.name) sections done (74db93a). 21 Oct review: `==` for records with proof fields is partly done (derived DecEq handles proofs of equations in DecEq types; other proof fields still E-INSTANCE-NONE, examples/reject/record-eqeq-proof-field.sw) -> SW-202; JS boundary proof fields for ordinary data types -> SW-203.

Done when: `theorem eta (p: Pair a b): p = (p.fst, p.snd) := rfl` checks for pairs and for a record, with the tests of records.md §14.

22 Oct 2026: D503 (Matt: yes) — build record eta after generated ext lemmas and glued values stage 1 land (both touch conversion).

Reminder (D1981, Matt, 30 Oct 2026): once proof irrelevance (SW-93) is built, record eta must apply only to records with at least one field that isn't a proof. A record whose fields are all proofs then behaves like a unit type, and eta on it breaks transitivity of conversion (docs/research/kernel.md §5.2; Lennon-Bertrand FSCD25, Rosain et al. POPL26; Rocq requires at least one relevant field). records.md §7.1 condition 4 should say so.

From SW-568 (merged, backlog review 4 Nov 2026): 'No eta for records in conversion': `p = { row = p.row, column = p.column }` needs a match on p. Sightings: rogue PROOFS.md, SW-960 (4), SW-990 (4), SW-999 (3). The D1981 reminder above is the same text. SW-789 stays as the decision; its 'D8: not now' is overtaken because at least four lanes have now needed eta, so SW-789 is the live question.

D2457 (Matt, 6 Nov 2026): yes, an Opus design note for kernel record eta, limited to records with at least one non-proof field (D1981), building on records.md §7. Ticket SW-789.

D2498-D2505 (Matt, 6 Nov 2026): all as recommended in docs/proposals/record-eta.md: kernel record eta with primitive projections (no parameters) and the two rules; eta by shape incl. Pair; no no-eta opt-out now; no eta for interface dictionaries; accept goals changing shape; keep T.ext; accept ~5% checking cost (profile it); staged kernel (Opus), unifier, Pair, clean-up sweep (Sonnet). Stages: SW-1642, SW-1643, SW-1644, SW-1645.

tickets.title: WebAssembly stack guard: measure limits in all browsers (incl. compact text) and choose the guard size
tickets.body:
Problem: each call uses stack in linear memory (which the guard measures) and the engine's own call stack (about 1 MiB in V8); the engine's runs out first, so the guard is 256 KiB (crates/web/build.rs, WASM_GUARD; override STITCHWORT_GUARD; it was 128 KiB until games/rogue's 11-field `State` was bundled), calibrated in Node and Chrome only. Firefox and Safari are unmeasured. 256 KiB gives about 25 levels of nesting and list literals of about 200 elements, with a margin of 2 only in Node/Chrome. The parser's stack use per level could also be cut (e.g. boxing `Diagnostic` in its `Result`): that is SW-126.

Change, one campaign: measure in all four engines with web/stress.html: nesting depth, long list/text literals (including compact `List Char` literals, d4d3626, which were only measured natively: the limit before E-RESOURCE and the time), then pick the guard size.

Eliminating recursion (stack-safe-evaluation steps 3 and 4, docs/proposals/stack-safe-evaluation.md) is the real fix; see also SW-62 (long literals) and SW-57 (JS limits in browsers, different subject: generated code).

Done when: a table of limits per browser (nesting, literal length, compact text) is in docs/evaluator-speed.md or compact-text.md and the guard is set from it.

History: split 19 Oct into SW-126; merged SW-61 (guard size) and SW-52 (compact text in WASM).


Closed in the 22 Nov board audit: duplicate of SW-3134 (SW-3134 is the same campaign (measure the engine stack per browser, set the guard, check Safari); crates/web/build.rs:37 WASM_GUARD is now 320 KiB, not the 256 KiB the body says). Audit note (22 Nov): Merged into SW-3134: also measure compact List Char literals and nesting depth in Firefox/Safari with web/stress.html.

tickets.title: Proof irrelevance stage 1: proof-position masks in conversion (D1′)
tickets.body:
Implement stage 1 of docs/proposals/proof-irrelevance.md (draft 5, 688de314c; D1′ with D2349, D2352-D2354, D1980). Opus. After SW-1226, before SW-1227 (D2348).

Order (one branch, commits per step, §9):
0. D1980 (§7.11): E-PROP-ELIM refuses a proposition whose constructor field mentions itself. Measure first (std builds, examples/ pass, `stitchwort check` on aoc/ and games/rogue: no E-PROP-ELIM); stop and report if anything relies on it. Test 26.
1. Marks: Def::inert_params (length = arity) and data proof_params, computed in install_group / declare_data on both checked and trusted paths (no check-cache format change); std listing; reference validator; native test (§7.3).
2. conv skips with J and arity boundaries; same_stuck_trees: all-impossible cases equal without comparing scrutinees; reference conv (§7.2).
3. Shortcut mode at K1-K4, CallMemo and TreeMemo keyed by mode, reference R1-R3 and EQUAL_CALLS (§7.2 table).
4. Unifier (§7.5): masks with the whole-metavariable rule via solve; mode at U1-U5.
5. Tests §8: 1-30 + 11b, unit tests, enumerated equivalence/gluing test, three-way runs (17-19, 24, 25, 27), mutations (temporary edits, results recorded here).
6. Docs: docs/core.md (rule, glued calls, precondition, D1981), DESIGN §6, doc comments (§7.4), unify_index.rs:184 comment, mutual-recursion.md §6.7.

Done when: all §8 tests pass and the three-way runs agree; each listed mutation fails its named tests (recorded here); sameMod (§2.1) and handBuilt (§2.2) check by rfl; std inert listing matches §7.3's table or differences are explained here; reference validator passes over std and test programs; bench: nothing >10% slower, anything >5% explained; hash snapshots unchanged or each change explained; merge tier green; daily-tier run (ask Matt first, D2348) green, including the STITCHWORT_GLUE=0 corpus run.

Expected: 480 min (step 0 ~45; marks+analysis ~120; skips+modes ~150; unifier ~60; tests ~90; docs ~15). Checkpoint report after step 0 and after step 3.

(Draft 3's body and the dialExt example were replaced 4 Nov by SW-1268's draft 5; dialExt no longer exists in aoc/.)

WARNING, read before starting (Matt, 30 Oct 2026; from the kernel research register, docs/research/kernel.md §5.1, read in full texts): the recursive-proposition trap. If a proposition can be eliminated into data AND holds a proof of itself in a field, definitional proof irrelevance makes conversion undecidable: any proof X can be unfolded once more, X ≡ MkLoop (Loop.inv X), with no bound on how many unfoldings conversion must try (Gilbert et al. POPL19 §2.3; Abel & Coquand; Lean answered with lean4#13851/#14977). Stitchwort accepts such a type TODAY: E-PROP-ELIM (crates/core/src/check.rs:915-929) lets a single-constructor Prop whose fields are all Prop eliminate into data, without asking whether a field mentions the type itself. Checked by the orchestrator on 30 Oct with main's binary: `type Loop: Prop = | MkLoop (next: Loop)` with `def steps (l: Loop): Nat := match l with | MkLoop n => Succ (steps n)` checks. It is harmless now (no definitional irrelevance yet), but becomes the trap once D1′ masks proof positions. proof-irrelevance.md §5.1 currently defends Loop by making D1′ deliberately incomplete; the register recommends closing the hole instead: add a condition to E-PROP-ELIM that no constructor field mentions the type itself (Lean's rule), after measuring that nothing in std, examples, AoC or rogue relies on it (register ticket T2; decision D1980, open). Do this BEFORE or AS PART OF stage 1, with Loop/steps as a must-reject test.


D1980 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): yes, refuse eliminating a self-referential proposition into data (the warning above), but as part of THIS ticket's work, not before it: when SW-93 starts, measure first that nothing in std, examples, AoC or rogue eliminates such a proposition into data, then add the E-PROP-ELIM condition with Loop/steps as a must-reject test.
Reminder (D1981, Matt, 30 Oct): record eta interacts with this ticket. Once proofs are irrelevant, a record whose fields are all proofs behaves like a unit type, and eta on it breaks transitivity of conversion (docs/research/kernel.md §5.2; Lennon-Bertrand FSCD25, Rosain et al. POPL26, Rocq requires a relevant field). If record eta (SW-55/SW-789) exists or lands after this, it must be limited to records with at least one field that isn't a proof.


D2348 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): yes, schedule as designed (docs/proposals/proof-irrelevance.md, D1-prime, decided 19 Oct). Opus. After SW-1226 merges, before SW-1227 (both touch the unifier). Merge tier plus a daily-tier run (ask Matt first). Then revisit D2180: if h: equations for any condition.


D2349 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): restrict masks at definitions' arguments to proof parameters the definition never computes on (no case, J or Quot.ind on it, only passed to other masked positions); constructor fields masked as before. Reason: glued calls (SW-257, after draft 3) compare same-head calls argument-first, so unrestricted masks reintroduce Carneiro's non-transitivity (steps l 0 / cast rfl x) and make gluing change what is accepted. D2350: draft 4 of the note first (SW-1250).


Decided by the orchestrator, delegated by Matt (4 Nov 2026: "above my pay grade - can you make good decisions?"), per note draft 4: D2352 yes (shortcut mode: inert arguments skipped, constructor proof fields compared); D2353 yes (an impossible case, as in Void.absurd, is not computing); D2354 yes (storing a proof parameter in a constructor field makes it non-inert); D2355 yes (independent Opus review of the new parts of 5.1, 5.7, 7.1-7.3, 7.10 before stage 1; to start when Matt lifts the hold on new lanes). tickets.title: Array type with get/set/length
tickets.body:
A compact native `Array a` with get/set/length (like compact text), proposed as capability #4 in docs/aoc-2025.md:688 for days 4, 8 and 9. The std library has `Vec` (length-indexed, std/Vec/Vec.sw) but it is a linked list, so access is O(n). Concrete use case (D107, 20 Oct 2026): AoC day 4 part 2 would use a worklist (remove a roll, recheck its 8 neighbours) with O(1) grid access; today `sweep` (aoc/src/Aoc/Day04/Day04.sw:112) walks the whole grid about 60 times (5 s). Large item: design note first (Opus), then a design review before building.

First step: measure whether it is really needed now that days 4 to 7 exist (aoc-2025.md says to measure after days 4-5) and whether `Vec`-based approaches suffice; then the design note (kernel representation, how it hashes, proofs about it, JS extraction as a JS array, and what `set` costs in a pure language: copy vs persistent structure).

Done when: the measurement and note exist and a build/don't-build decision is recorded; building is a separate ticket.

History: D107; aoc-2025.md capability #4.

22 Oct 2026 (day 4 research, D427): day 4 doesn't need a native array — the committed Vec program runs in 0.61 s, a Set worklist in 1.65 s. If an array is built, it should carry its length in the type (bjornestol's Lean day 4 spends ~60 lines of Array.set lemmas keeping rows rectangular). docs/comparisons/aoc-day04-community.md.

24 Oct 2026 (board review): wording update. `sweep` (Day04.sw:112) no longer exists: Day 4 now settles with settleRows over Vec (aoc/src/Aoc/Day04/Day04.sw:99, decreasing, SW-276). Days 4 to 9 all exist, so the "measure first" step can be answered from them.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: the motivating paragraph above is out of date. `sweep` and Aoc/Day04/Day04.sw:112 no longer exist (Day 4 is now under aoc/src/Aoc/Year2024/Day04/; `settle` became `decreasing`, 904029fba, SW-276); the 5 s figure is from before. First step now: re-measure Day 4 part 2 (2024) and 2025 days 4/8/9. SW-808 now lists 'array with constant-time indexing' as a DUPLICATE of this ticket, so this is the survivor. Related motivation: SW-813, SW-814 (interpreter and Map speed).

Same request as SW-1473 (array design note, docs/proposals/arrays.md, 6 Nov 2026); closed into it.

tickets.title: Constructor names: should they live inside their type (Quit vs GaveUp ambiguity), or be resolved by expected type?
tickets.body:
The problem: constructors of different union types share one namespace, so two types cannot both have a constructor `Quit`. The roguelike renamed its `Quit` to `GaveUp` for this reason (D2, NOTES stage 1 #8; unchecked wording).

The change: a design discussion with Matt first. Options: constructors nested in their type (`Outcome.Quit`), or resolving a bare name by the expected type, or leaving as is and documenting the rename trick.

What it should do: Matt picks one; if the answer is not "leave as is", a design note in docs/proposals/ follows. Label it `decision` so it shows up.

Raised by SW-3339: a lexer and a printer in one program (token Str vs layout Str) make | Str t => ambiguous even where the match's type is known; the toy formatter will hit it.

Opus paper started 12:00, expected 1.5 h: design note docs/proposals/constructor-names.md ahead of the full formatter.

12:10 review: docs/proposals/constructor-names.md written (not committed). Probed today: bare clashing constructors are E-AMBIGUOUS in patterns, values, arguments, lists, record updates and comparisons even with the type known; a file's own `None` breaks `| None` on an Option. Options (a) expected type first, (a') type as tie-break, (b) `.Ctor` only, (c) both, (d) status quo. Recommends (a): the known type's constructor wins, ambiguous names wait on the queue when the type isn't known yet; terms and hashes unchanged. Four stages, ~8-9 h (Sonnet 1.5 h, Opus 2 h, Opus 2-3 h, Sonnet 1.5 h). Question: D3615 (adopt (a)? rec yes).


D3615 (Matt, 15 Nov 2026): "option one plus a discipline to avoid files that need to import multiple clashing names unless it's code that genuinely must use both. The code organization habit. We can maybe think about going back to this dot shorthand as Lean does in three in the future, potentially. But yeah, for now, let's proceed with your suggestion." Not type-directed resolution (Matt: one name, one meaning per file, readable at a glance). Built as SW-3397; .C shorthand parked as SW-3398.

tickets.title: Parameter untupling: ((row, chars) => ...) where a function on pairs is expected
tickets.body:
The problem: a lambda written with two parameters is refused where a function on pairs is expected, so `.map ((row, chars) => ...)` needs `.map (((row, chars)) => ...)` (extra brackets). Scala 3 splits the pair automatically ("parameter untupling", https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/reference/other-new-features/parameter-untupling.html). Found in the roguelike port (NOTES stage 1 #10).

The change: when a lambda with n>1 parameters is checked against a one-argument function on an n-tuple, treat it as a pattern lambda over the tuple.

What it should do: `[(1, "a")].map ((n, s) => ...)` is accepted and means the same as the bracketed form; arities that don't match still give the usual error. Needs Matt's go-ahead because it is a syntax rule.

Board audit (5 Nov 2026): obsolete: xs.map ((a, b) => a + b) checks today; docs/proposals/lambda-syntax.md calls untupling moot. Closed.

tickets.title: Roguelike per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: step calls next() once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) …, Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling roll freely. Why: then seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants (walls, HP, occupancy, stepValid, replayValid) are proved about pure resolve for every seed. Free roll would lose them until proofs through a handler stop stepping symbolically into E-RESOURCE (see the handler-stepping ticket; Effect.bindAssoc axiom). Idea (untested): state invariants for any answers to roll rather than via seeded. Revert to free roll once provable (D1305, Matt 26 Oct)

tickets.title: Interpreter speed: about 6.5 ns per instruction is the main cost in every AoC day (20-100x slower than Python on generated inputs)
tickets.body:
Map lane profile (28 Oct): ~2,060 of 3,000 samples in the machine's main loop, then value freeing and register-vector resizing. Day 19: ~11M small closure calls dominate 8.1 s. Investigate dispatch, frame setup and register allocation before data-structure work.

Design done, merged: docs/proposals/interpreter-speed.md. Cost is the work around each instruction (calls/returns ~900 host instructions), not dispatch; keep the match loop and shared bytecode; est. 1.5-2x on Map/Set days, 2-3x on call-heavy code. D3060 yes (orchestrator's call: no unsafe in the machine for now). D3061 (about four lane-days worth it?) goes to Matt with stage 0b's profile. Stages SW-2129..SW-2135, SW-2136. Day 19's 8.1 s is out of date (SW-1636: 2.3 s).

tickets.title: Memory: resources test reaches 6.7 GB loading one small program repeatedly (sessions not freed?); lsp aoc_navigation test 7.9 GB
tickets.where: lane (D2079): daily tier time + resources memory
tickets.body:
Found while getting the daily tier green (31 Oct 2026). Measured alone with /usr/bin/time -l (peak memory footprint), STITCHWORT_TIER=daily:
- crates/driver/tests/resources.rs `running_out_at_any_point_only_ever_means_no_answer`: 6.7 GB on main (6.35 GB at 6e25695e, 28 Oct). It loads one small PROGRAM in a fresh `Session::new()` at every work limit from 1 up, so peak memory should be about one session. 6.7 GB suggests sessions (or something global they register: interned names, metas, caches, Rc cycles) aren't freed when dropped. A long-running language server creating sessions would leak the same way. Find what grows per iteration (e.g. measure footprint every N iterations) and fix the leak.
- crates/cli/tests/lsp.rs `aoc_navigation_matches_check_index`: 7.9 GB on main, 33 s (9.9 GB, 176 s on 28 Oct, so better than it was). Find whether that's inherent (the whole AoC project in the LSP plus check --index) or held longer than needed.
Together they took `task test:daily` past its 16 GB cap. Workaround merged tonight: the resources test (and rt's aoc_agrees / every_aoc_main_lowers, which are AoC sweeps) joined the `corpus-sweeps` one-at-a-time group in .config/nextest.toml. docs/testing.md's table still says the daily peak is "not measured".


D2079 (Matt, 31 Oct 2026): lane to cut the daily tier toward 5 min. Evidence: daily 606 s of tests; the one-at-a-time corpus-sweeps group took 562 s over 33 tests run serially; resources 109 s and fmt_hashes 102 s are a third of it. Do: sparser fmt_hashes daily sample; SW-921 (why the resources test holds 6.7 GB and takes 109 s); re-time the tier.


Lane progress (31 Oct): the resources test runs 161 work limits. Not a leak: after each session drops, the Rust heap is back at 30 MB (counting allocator). Limits 2075 to 8166 (about 30 of them) make about 50 library theorems fail; each failure runs a counterexample search whose fast-runtime recursion grows the machine's register Vec to 162 MB (240 MB live at the peak, about 1 s per session). macOS's system malloc keeps those freed large blocks in its large cache: RSS +229 MB per such session, about 6 GB in all. With MallocLargeCache=0, RSS stays at 61 MB; with mimalloc (which the CLI and language server use), at 345 MB. Fix: the test uses mimalloc, and the daily tier samples the work limits.

Lane progress: the time is the counterexample searches (cargo's env sets STITCHWORT_UNTIMED_COUNTEREXAMPLES=1, so there's no 200 ms backstop): with it, 107 s for all 161 limits, without it, 37 s. Change: the test samples its limits with tier_sample(…, 4) (daily 25 s at load 33, 364 MB; full 107 s, 367 MB, was 5.2 to 6.7 GB) and has left corpus-sweeps. fmt_hashes: 137 of its 160 s was the AoC project (two whole loads on one thread), now full only; files and projects every 8th: 22 s at load 24, 217 MB (was 115 to 160 s, 2.0 GB). Both pass in daily and full. Re-timing the daily tier next.

Lane done: commit 2c13d892 on worktree-agent-a900b8669314821d6. Daily tier re-timed at load 7 to 80 (other lanes running): 599 s of tests, all 1766 passed, memguard peak 11.5 GB. The load roughly doubled other tests' times (rewind examples 32 to 61 s), so this doesn't compare with the 606 s quiet run. resources went from 109 to 53 s and left the serial group; fmt_hashes went from 102 to 21 s. Without them the serial group is about 350 s of quiet time, so the tier is still over 5 min. Next candidates are the sweeps with no sample: erasure, run_js, run_reference, cli examples accepted/rejected, std_library core_alone, fuzz_elab, rt lower/machine examples (stride 2 to 4 each); rewind examples 8 to 16; differential 4 to 8. tickets.title: Proof hashes differ between debug and release builds (float-playlist example)
tickets.body:
Found 1 Nov 2026 while merging AoC day 10. examples/accept/float-playlist.sw's proofs hash differently in debug and release builds, every run:
- `cargo nextest run --release -p stitchwort-driver --test hash_stability examples` passes (Main.nextStartNotEarlier 460aa8c3…).
- the same without --release fails: nextStartNotEarlier 087ab8f8…, startTimesAscend and playlistAscends also differ. Repeated twice, same values.
So the elaborated proof term depends on the build profile. Hashes are meant to depend only on content.
Untraced suspects: `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` code in elab: queue.rs:1302 `assert_rule_closed` (runs head_meta on waiting items in a debug build only; if that forces or fills a meta, terms can differ) and rows.rs:742; or a float computation that differs in debug.
Impact: merge tier runs --release so it's green; a lane running hash_stability in debug sees a false failure. Correctness: debug assertions must not change what is elaborated.

1 Nov (Opus lane, commit a515d3e1 on worktree-agent-a0344c35ed5b905d8): cause found. Not debug_assertions (skipping assert_rule_closed changed nothing). 41 std declarations hash differently in debug (Std.Nat.partitionPointBounds first; float-playlist inherits it via Float.addMonotoneRight). Cheap attempts that are taken as "no" when they fail (unify::cheaply's let refolding, omega/ring atom comparisons, closing/search match attempts) each had their own 128 KiB / 4 MiB stack budget in bytes; debug frames are bigger, so cheaply failed 790 times in debug vs 7 in release. Fix: Budget::attempt keeps the enclosing operation's stack floor (steps/size/frames limits are the same in every build); an attempt that reaches the floor ends the operation. Regression test: builtins::the_library_hashes_as_in_the_release_build (debug-builtins gate) + 2 budget unit tests. Release hashes unchanged (std, aoc, examples); all examples now match in debug.

tickets.title: BUG: cases panics (value.rs:1011 index underflow) when a proof stops matching the program
tickets.body:
Found by the AoC 2021 day 16 lane (1 Nov 2026), confirmed on main's release binary: `stitchwort check` on the repro below panics at crates/core/src/value.rs:1011:31 "index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 18446744073709551615" (an index underflow, likely a de Bruijn shift). In the repo: flip `if more` to `if not more` in Day16's readGroups, then `stitchwort check Aoc.Year2021.Day16.Proofs`. It happens when a `cases` proof stops matching the program, i.e. exactly when an agent breaks the program on purpose (proving-guide rule 6). Should be an error, never a panic; add the repro to examples/reject once fixed.

Repro (74 lines):
import Std (Bool, DecEq, Eq, List, Nat, Option, Pair, Void)



def readGroups: List Bool → Option (List Nat, List Bool)
  | Cons more (Cons a (Cons b (Cons c (Cons d rest)))) =>
    let group := Nat.fromBits [a, b, c, d]
    if not more then
      match readGroups rest with
        | Some (groups, after) => Some (Cons group groups, after)
        | None => None
    else Some ([group], rest)
  | _ => None

def bitsOf: Nat → Nat → List Bool
  | 0, _ => Nil
  | Succ width, n => bitsOf width (n / 2) ++ [n % 2 == 1]

def groupBits: List Nat → List Bool
  | Nil => Nil
  | Cons group Nil => Cons False (bitsOf 4 group)
  | Cons group rest => Cons True (bitsOf 4 group ++ groupBits rest)

theorem halfOfDouble (acc: Nat) (bit: Bool): (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) / 2 = acc :=
  let split := Nat.divModEq (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  let below := Nat.modLess (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  match bit with
    | True => omega
    | False => omega

theorem parityOfDouble (acc: Nat) (bit: Bool): ((acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) % 2 == 1) = bit :=
  let split := Nat.divModEq (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  let below := Nat.modLess (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  match bit with
    | True =>
      let odd: (acc * 2 + 1) % 2 = 1 := omega
      rewrite odd in rfl
    | False =>
      let even: (acc * 2 + 0) % 2 = 0 := omega
      rewrite even in rfl

theorem bitsOfFold (k: Nat): (acc: Nat) → (bits: List Bool) →
    bitsOf (k + bits.length) (List.foldLeft bits acc (acc bit => acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit)) = bitsOf k acc ++ bits
  | acc, Nil => rewrite Nat.addZero k, List.appendNil (bitsOf k acc) in rfl
  | acc, Cons bit rest =>
    let more := bitsOfFold (Succ k) (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) rest
    let step: bitsOf (Succ k) (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) ++ rest = bitsOf k acc ++ Cons bit rest :=
      rewrite parityOfDouble acc bit, halfOfDouble acc bit, List.appendAssoc (bitsOf k acc) [bit] rest in rfl
    Eq.trans more step

theorem bitsOfFromBits (bits: List Bool): bitsOf bits.length (Nat.fromBits bits) = bits := bitsOfFold 0 0 bits

theorem fromBitsBelow (bits: List Bool): Nat.fromBits bits < Nat.pow 2 bits.length := omega [Nat.fromBitsFlipped bits]


theorem somePairInjective (x1: a) (y1: b) (x2: a) (y2: b) (h: Some (x1, y1) = Some (x2, y2)): x1 = x2 ∧ y1 = y2 :=
  let both := Option.someInjective _ _ h
  Both (Pair.mkInjectiveFst _ _ _ _ both) (Pair.mkInjectiveSnd _ _ _ _ both)

theorem readGroupsSome: (bits: List Bool) → (groups: List Nat) → (rest: List Bool) → readGroups bits = Some (groups, rest) →
    bits = groupBits groups ++ rest ∧ groups ≠ Nil ∧ groups.all (group => group < 16) = True
  | Cons more (Cons a (Cons b (Cons c (Cons d tail)))), groups, rest, read =>
    let written: bitsOf 4 (Nat.fromBits [a, b, c, d]) = [a, b, c, d] := bitsOfFromBits [a, b, c, d]
    match more with
      | True =>
        match e: readGroups tail with
          | None => cases
          | Some (gs, after) => ?
      | False => ?
  | Nil, groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ Nil, groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ (Cons _ Nil), groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ (Cons _ (Cons _ Nil)), groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ (Cons _ (Cons _ (Cons _ Nil))), groups, rest, read => cases

Progress (Opus lane, 1 Nov): cause found and fixed in 09a54de6 (branch worktree-agent-a492afefe71463e04). cases.rs take_apart evaluated a constructor field's type under the parameters only, but field types are stored under params + earlier fields: Cons's tail `List a` underflowed (the panic); a pair's `snd: b` was read as `a` (wrong-typed fact: a type mismatch, or a fact that missed the goal). Env is now params ++ left side's earlier fields. No other caller shares the pattern. Regression: examples/reject/cases-later-field.sw, examples/accept/cases-later-field.sw. Repro and Day16 flip now give errors, no panic (repro: E-CASES-BUDGET after ~100 s release, cases splitting Nat.divStep internals; a separate perf issue).

tickets.title: Doc links: resolve in doc/index with the file's imports; cached W-DOC-LINK can go stale across namespaces
tickets.body:
Known limits from SW-1042 (accepted for now, 1 Nov 2026): (1) doc and check --index resolve links without the file's imports (they don't elaborate), so a link that only an import makes resolve gets no W-DOC-LINK from check but shows unresolved in doc and null in the index; (2) W-DOC-LINK is cached with the namespace check and links add no dependency, so a cached warning about a link into another namespace can go stale until that namespace changes or --no-cache; (3) the nearest-name suggestion scans every name in scope (~2 ms per unresolved link).


Fixed in 3e9d7b8a (lane/SW-1100): doc/index resolve links through the file's import lines (syntactic, no elaboration); W-DOC-LINK no longer cached, recomputed after every check and replay (old entries' warnings dropped). Tests: a_link_an_import_makes_resolve_resolves_in_doc_and_the_index, a_cached_link_warning_follows_the_namespace_it_points_into.

function_equations a_match_below_a_lifted_alternative_refines_where_its_variable_is_bound fails: deeper.eq2.some.nil not generated (after SW-1077 / de25c46e)
tickets.body:
Known failing daily-tier test at push (2 Nov 2026): stitchwort-driver::function_equations a_match_below_a_lifted_alternative_refines_where_its_variable_is_bound — `deeper.eq2.some.nil` isn't generated (function_equations.rs:109). SW-1069's nested-match case (def deeper: `Cons x rest => match List.head rest with | Some y => match rest with | Nil => x | Cons z more => y + z | None => 1`).

It passed when SW-1069/1071 merged (lane ran it), so SW-1077 (closed-condition skip, CLOSED_SPLIT in crates/elab/src/equations.rs) or de25c46e (the if h: condition fix to that skip) probably broke it. Tried and reverted (didn't fix it): exempting a constructor-headed scrutinee from the match-side closed check (equations.rs ~2965). Cause unknown. A missing equation, not unsoundness.

Next: bisect SW-1077's merge vs de25c46e with only this test plus branch_equations, an_overlapped_arms_branches_are_read_from_each_case, the_walls_errors_name_the_branch_equations; fix; rerun only those (Matt: strict test budget).


Cause (found 2 Nov 2026, Speedwell, by reading the code; no bisect run needed): SW-1077's match-side CLOSED_SPLIT check (bf554bea). de25c46e only touched the if-side check, and deeper has no if. For eq2.some.nil the first run asks to refine rest (bound in the row) to Nil; in the refined run the outer scrutinee List.head rest becomes List.head Nil, which is closed, so the branch was skipped. The test expects exactly that closed hypothesis (isSome: List.head [] = Some y). The earlier constructor-head exemption missed it because List.head Nil is headed by a Def.

Fix (uncommitted in the working tree): both CLOSED_SPLIT checks in branch_run (if and match) apply only when refines is empty, i.e. on the unrefined run, which meets any term that is closed in the program first. Trade-off: a split that is closed in the program and lies below the step where the first run stopped to ask for a refinement is now stated, not skipped. That costs kernel work but is sound, and the case is narrow.

Tests run: function_equations, the 4 targeted tests (a_match_below..., branch_equations, an_overlapped_arms..., the_walls_errors...): 4/4 ok. rustfmt clean. Hashes lane tier (STITCHWORT_TIER=lane, profile lane-hashes: hash_stability examples/projects/prelude + pinned_hashes): 5/5 passed, so no snapshot changes. Ready to commit.

tickets.title: search --at on a goal mentioning ≤ (cli test what_closes_a_goal) elaborates most of the library (Float, Int, Char files...), 1.4 GB live; find why lazy loading pulls it in and load only what the search needs (found by SW-1076)
tickets.body:
Analysis (read-only Explore agent, 2 Nov 2026; code read, nothing run; medium confidence on the mechanism):
- Loading isn't the difference: search --at loads all std up front for every goal (load_all_libraries, crates/cli/src/main.rs:1857; driver search_at.rs:1567, :1670). Goals 1/3 0.29 GB vs goal 2 1.5 GB comes from searching and checking.
- closing_plans turns the constants filter off (filter: false, crates/elab/src/closing.rs:365), so every declaration is unified with the goal. ≤ on Nat is the built-in Nat.LessEq, which unfolds to `… = True`, so any `_ = True` conclusion matches, including generated equations from unrelated files (closing.rs:421-424 cites Char.isAsciiSpaceCode.eq1 closing a Float.ieeeLe goal). Each match gets several plans (hypotheses h1, h2) and each is tried with rfl/omega/cases/byDecision (search_at.rs:1250); search.md:1165 records one cases check at 1.2 GB.
- Memory held: Globals defs/datas (core/src/globals.rs:421), whole-library generated equations (search_at.rs:612), lifted <input N> definitions kept per check (lib.rs:1178); nothing freed until main.rs:1888.
- Levers: filter on in closing_plans (or overlaps, search.rs:893) with the relaxed second pass as fallback; skip generated equations sharing no data type with the goal; load only the goal's needs (library.rs:1002 load_needs); per-check memory/step caps or no cases on obligations (today time only, search_at.rs:541).
Plan when picked up (Opus): confirm with STITCHWORT_SEARCH_DEBUG per-check timings; then the filter with fallback; report memory and the AoC closing rate (66% today, SW-915) before/after. The recall benchmark is beyond targeted tests: agree the test strategy with Matt first (D2198, Matt 2 Nov: backlog for now).

Done 8f7c0db7 (Sonnet, 40 min, est. 45), reviewed, merged. The analysis above was wrong: = True matching is not the cost (4525 candidates, 64 matched, 50 tried, 382 checks). tickets.title: Experiment (D2202 b, D2203): the same loose brief to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Sonnet for three tasks of rising difficulty (SW-926 easy, SW-1081 medium, SW-1073 hard), to find where each model's work can be trusted. Score per run: correctness (line-by-line review), completeness, rules followed, wall time, cost; merge the best run of a task only if useful and Matt agrees
tickets.body:
Results (2 Nov 2026). Same loose brief per task (D2202 b); DeepSeek via opencode run in a scratch clone, Sonnet as a general-purpose subagent; from pair 2 on, both briefs say "never run a command in the background".

| Task | Sonnet | DeepSeek |
|---|---|---|
| SW-926 easy (diagnostic note) | correct minimal fix, good test passes, 3 snapshots; one slip (started a full sweep, killed it). 6 min, 55k tokens | same fix, nearly identical code; its test FAILS (one wrong case, never run); unfinished: backgrounded its build and the one-shot run ended, no report. 7.5 min |
| SW-1081 medium (destructuring let equations) | correct, narrow (tuple/record only); existing examples unchanged; example + doc test. 15 min, 79k tokens | correct, broader (proof-ctor lets too, kernel-checked); caught the change to an existing example and left the snapshot; specific skip reason; updated the design note. 15 min |
| SW-1073 hard, narrowed (List.unfold.induct) | works: all induct tests incl. library and AoC sweeps pass; also handles doubly nested patterns. 26 min, 123k tokens | works: same tests pass; nested pattern in the last field only. 31 min |

Findings:
- On code, DeepSeek matched Sonnet at all three levels given a loose brief; Sonnet's solutions were somewhat more general on the hard task, DeepSeek's more thorough on the medium one.
- DeepSeek's failures were process, not reasoning: a one-shot opencode run can't wait on a backgrounded command (fixed by one brief line), and it shipped a test it never ran.
- Neither diff can be trusted without review; the hard task's kernel-term code needs an Opus line-by-line review before merging either.
Suggested boundary: DeepSeek (with "never background", "run every test you add") for tasks up to medium elaborator work from a goal-level brief; Sonnet where generality and judgement on a design matter (kernel-adjacent generators), or where a wrong guess spreads. Small sample: three tasks, one run each.
Mergeable: SW-926 Sonnet's; SW-1081 DeepSeek's (broader) or Sonnet's (smaller); SW-1073 either after review (Sonnet's more general). Matt to choose.

tickets.title: Research: Osprey's effects (https://www.ospreylang.dev/docs/effects/) - what it is, and what Stitchwort's abilities/handlers could borrow
tickets.body:
Result (Opus research lane, 2 Nov 2026; read-only). Osprey: functional language in Rust -> LLVM by one author (Nimblesite), repo since June 2025, v0.28, ~65 stars, spec well ahead of what's built; a credible prototype, not a reference design. Effects: per-operation modes (value vs control abort/once/many), deep handlers, handler values or block-scoped `handle`, rows by inclusion (open rows a prototype), `handle static` (compile-time discharge or error), Arith effect, replayable, finally/mask/instance (mostly planned).
Stitchwort already same or better: direct style, deep handlers, return clause, unhandled = compile error, row polymorphism built (effect-polymorphism.md 0-3), multi-shot on every runner (D1162), kernel-checked handler termination via Effect.Comp/foldComp (DESIGN §8), handler-based testing plus proofs; Arith not needed (unbounded numbers, / needs a proof).
Candidates, ranked: (1) a "handle static"-style assertion that a handler takes the fused/in-place fast path or says which clause stopped it (fusion.rs reasons; would have caught SW-861): worth doing, as evidence for research T5 (docs/research/effects.md §6). (2) declared operation modes (Koka fun/ctl, Osprey abort/once): maybe, add to SW-791/D1428's options; also answers DESIGN §16 Q9 for JS extraction. (3) differential tests of handler semantics against Koka (nixpkgs koka 3.2.9; port examples/accept/abilities.sw and row tests): worth a low-priority ticket, it checks the trusted translation independently. (4) requirement provenance in diagnostics/hover (Store@3:15.get): maybe, fold into research rank 6. No: mask/named instances (abilities.md:229), finally/replayable, block-scoped handle / second syntax.
Sources: ospreylang.dev/docs/effects/, /spec/0017-algebraiceffects/, /status/, github.com/Nimblesite/osprey (examples/handlers, docs/plans/0016-algebraic-effects-and-handlers.md).

tickets.title: Research: mold linker (https://github.com/rui314/mold) as a quick win for Stitchwort's Rust builds on this Mac and Linux: does it support macOS, how much of our build/test time is linking, what would wiring it in cost
tickets.body: Result (Sonnet research lane, 2 Nov 2026): not worth wiring in. mold is ELF-only now (Mach-O support removed; the macOS port continues commercially as sold); nixpkgs mold 3.0.0 evaluates on aarch64-darwin but can't link Mach-O. Measured here (release, no kache): linking is ~0.4-0.5 s of a 15 s incremental rebuild (touch crates/cli: ~3%), 0.43 s of a 113 s test-binary rebuild (<0.4%); a clean build makes 44 links of ~0.3 s each in parallel. ld-prime and ld64.lld no different (noise, ±0.1-0.2 s). Note: the devShell's linker is nix's ld64-956.6, not Apple's ld-prime. Linux: mold would save at most tenths of a second per 16-22 MB binary; not worth it (musl static path, reproducibility). If Linux links ever take seconds: [target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'] link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold in .cargo/config.toml plus pkgs.mold/clang in the Linux devShell; measure with --timings first. Build time is rustc/LLVM codegen.

Options (1 wall-s ~ 8.4 CPU-s; 60 s needs ~500 CPU-s cut): (1) revise the budget for this machine (no coverage cost); (2) hash_stability examples/projects sweeps to daily or sampled (17-20 s / ~10 s); (3) halve aoc_answers (7-10 s); (4) goal_index and part of the search family to their lane profiles only (~22 s); (5) cli examples sample every 8th (~8 s); (6) split/schedule the long tail (up to ~10 s, no coverage cost); (7) profile slow code: hash_stability, extract generated_code_is_stable (7 s solo, docs say ~4 s).

tickets.title: Build speed through crate and compilation architecture (D2201): edit-rebuild time is dominated by recompiling large crates (crates/elab ~188k lines) in release mode without incremental compilation; linking is negligible (SW-1086). Measure what a one-line edit costs to rebuild in elab and in core (today, and with incremental release), then propose the end-state architecture (crate splits, profiles, codegen units, generated code, test-binary layout, dev vs release for tests) that gives the fastest edit-test loop; migration cost secondary (Matt). Design note first if it proposes restructuring
tickets.body:
Phase 1 (Opus, 2 Nov 2026; analysis only, nothing built). Correction: elab is 99k lines of .rs (plus 28k of embedded std .sw), not 188k. The cost of an edit is mostly fan-out: ~165 test binaries, ~135 depend on elab; lanes build all of them because test:one/test:lane run `nextest --workspace` (nextest builds every binary before filtering). A std .sw edit rebuilds the whole stack (include_str! plus driver/build.rs's fingerprint). Dev-dependency-only features (core reference/stack-check, syntax stack-check, rt alloc-trace) likely make `task build` and test builds compile the stack twice (inferred). elab also compiles twice per edit (lib and lib-test, 124 unit tests). Inside elab: 58 of 77 modules (89k lines) are one strongly connected cluster around `impl Elaborator`; no cheap split. Not significant: proc macros (none), generics, build scripts, linking. Release is needed for stack depth (debug ~10x larger frames) and sweep speed.
Ranked: (1) lanes build only the targets they run (--workspace --test X / --lib); (2) one feature set for all builds; (3) std read from disk in dev/test, embedded only in distributed builds (design note); (4) tuned test profile: release + incremental + more codegen units, maybe lower opt-level for elab/tests (measure; stack and kache risks); (5) one test binary per test package (design note); (6) elab's unit tests out of the lib; (7) split elab only if still on the critical path after 1-6. Not on stable: Cranelift, parallel front end.
End state: incremental tuned test profile, one binary per test package, lanes build what they run, one feature set, std from disk except in distributed builds, elab split only if measured necessary. Order 1, 2, 4, 3, 6, 5, then 7.
Measurement plan M0-M8 (~50-60 min machine time on a quiet machine, scratch checkout, kache off, nothing committed); M5's merge-tier comparison needs Matt's approval. Script: scratchpad modgraph.py.


D2210 (Matt, 2 Nov 2026): measurement phase deferred. Back to backlog; phase 1 above stands.

D2248 (Matt, 3 Nov): yes to the architecture review step 1 (docs/research/architecture-review.md): one feature set for every dev and test build (reference, stack-check, alloc-trace on in all of them; only distributed builds differ), measuring alloc-trace cost first (run-time switch if it costs), together with lanes building only what they run. tickets.title: Memory grows ~5.8 KB per input character in Std.Parse loops, fused or not (D2215 b, from SW-1087; noted on SW-861): Parse.next over 160,000 chars peaks 1.2-1.6 GB against 94 MB for the input list; a fused Nat-state handler at 1M operations peaks 6.3 GB. Find what is retained per operation (trail, continuation, sharing, allocator) and fix it. Sonnet; measure on a quiet machine
tickets.body:
Diagnosis (Sonnet, 2 Nov 23:40; no fix, no commit). Not the runtime: the checker. A `match` in `main` on a long effectful call (`match C.run (...) 0 with ...`) is fully evaluated at check time by `matching::generalised_now` -> `normals` (crates/elab/src/matching.rs) with core::value::run (no fusion, no tail resumption), ~7.3-7.8 KB per op, to test whether the scrutinee occurs in the goal. `check cn1m.sw` alone: 7.36 GB, 17 s. Moving the match into a helper (`show (C.run ...)`): cn1m 7.36 GB/18 s -> 69.5 MB/1.0 s; next (160k chars) 1.39 GB/4.6 s -> 101.8 MB/0.43 s; machine slope ~0.06 KB/char (the input list). Machine is bounded (frames=1). Not the allocator, not a leak (alloc-trace).
Consequence: SW-861 and SW-738's natural-vs-workaround memory comparisons measured the checker, not the fused machine; --js pays it too.
Proposed fix (needs Opus + Matt): in `normals`, return None (as the existing size cap does) when the scrutinee can't occur: closed, of an inductive Data type, and no constructor of it in the goal, hypothesis types or other scrutinees' types; or a work budget. Plus a regression test on check's peak memory. Longer term: fusion/tail resumption in core::value. Workaround: pass the handled result through a helper. Scratch helper-form programs: scratchpad/sw-1096/.
Model result: Sonnet, worked (diagnosis), 10 min (est. 45).


D2229 (Matt, 3 Nov): yes, fix it, starting with a brief literature review / rival implementation check (what Lean etc. do when generalising a match scrutinee). Opus lane.

Regression rows in crates/bench/tests/check_work.rs (evaluation steps constant in cost). Literature note docs/proposals/match-generalisation-evaluation.md: Lean 4 kabstract never evaluates the discriminant; Agda/Idris normalise like Stitchwort; recommends not moving to Lean's way now (a language decision for Matt). Opus review running.

Suspects (unconfirmed): two servers starting at once (SW-1092's run was alive at the first hang), the long-lived 'opencode serve --service' sharing opencode.db, 2.1.4 (earlier runs were 2.1.1). tickets.body:
Hang 3, 23:17:46 (run a225c46a, SW-1102 in a new scratch clone scratch-sw-1102): same signature, server 92c3af4c logged 'cli starting' and nothing in 2 min. Result (Sonnet, 2 Nov 23:41): cause found. With stdin not a terminal, opencode run waits for stdin EOF even with the prompt as an argument; an open pipe that never closes hangs it exactly as seen (server 'cli starting' then nothing). Repro: open pipe 2/2 hang; </dev/null 16/16 fine (reruns, fresh clones, production flags). Upstream anomalyco/opencode#59287 (open; triage says still on dev); 2.2.5 (nixpkgs-unstable) likely still hangs (fake-model test). Project.resolve stack was the idle server's startup fiber being cancelled. Not the serve --service process, not concurrency, not 2.1.4 (the wait is in v1 too, #38723). opencode comes from home.packages in ~/.config/nix-darwin/home/matt.nix:28. Workaround applied: </dev/null in CLAUDE.md and docs/workflow.md. Close after a few real runs start cleanly with it.

tickets.title: Daily tier takes 20.7 min against its 5-minute budget: what is slowing it
tickets.body:
Daily run 2 Nov 23:54-00:15 on a quiet machine: 1956/1956 passed, 20.7 min wall, nextest Summary 1056.9 s; the Taskfile says under 5 minutes. The machine went from 14 to 10 cores (SW-1090). D2230 (Matt, 3 Nov): Sonnet investigation of what is slowing it. Data: target/nextest/daily/junit.xml, copy in the orchestrator's scratchpad junit-daily-1.xml; log daily.log.

Findings (Sonnet, 3 Nov, 26 min, est. 40). Wall 1244 s: nextest 1057 s (85%), builtins debug 84 s, web:pkg 37 s, fmt/clippy ~25 s. CPU 9293 s, ~870 s wall at perfect packing on 10 cores (82% efficient); 5 min needs ~70% less CPU.
- Critical path: corpus-sweeps group (max-threads 1), 38 tests, 999 s serial, 36 s -> 1057 s; last 400 s ran on 1-3 cores. lsp group (lsp-aoc-copy, max-threads 1): 680 s; a_newer_edit_cancels_the_check_running 342 s, aoc_navigation_matches_check_index 245 s.
- Tests >= 10 s: 133 tests, 76% of test time. Top CPU: search_at_on_aoc_goals 500, rewind examples 467, accepted_examples_check 292, erasure 288, every_day_from_the_whole_projects_cache 159 (one thread).
- Since the budget (25 Oct, 3adb2672): it was never met after that; 606 s on 31 Oct (14 cores), 1057 s now. Tests 1766 -> 1956; search_at_aoc + soundness_fuzz added ~185 s to the serial group; the other sweeps ~2.2x (machine change + 8-thread pools contending; split not measured).
Proposals, ranked: (1) overlap the sweep chain (max-threads 2 or smaller pools; nextest priority), ~150-190 s, no coverage cost, needs a memory check; (2) LSP chain: priority, drop the group for tests not using the AoC copy, smaller namespace (SW-1094), up to 340 s off the path; (3) sample/move to full: search_at_aoc, rewind /4-/8, erasure stride 4, cli examples stride 2-4, every_day_from_the_whole_projects_cache, web every_aoc_day, operators lowering: ~1500 CPU-s, costs coverage; (4) share Session::eager_for_stack per binary (136 tests, ~1136 s test time; unmeasured); (5) builtins debug: move the two 60 s hash tests to release, skip web:pkg when fresh, ~70-80 s; (6) restate the budget for a 10-core M1 Pro after the above.


D2231 (Matt, 3 Nov): do 1 (overlap sweeps), 2 (LSP chain), 5 (builtins debug, web:pkg) and measure 4 (shared eager session); 3 (sampling) decided after. Test budget: targeted runs and the merge tier in the lane; the orchestrator runs one daily tier after merging to measure. Sonnet lane.


Implementation (Sonnet, 43 min, est. 60), merged 7f44deed (lane 04f66ce4):

tickets.body:
Found in SW-1096 (3 Nov): after the scrutinee fix, next.sw (Parse.next over 160,000 chars, the input bound by let input) still costs 395 MB at check time, ~1.9 KB per char. A sampled profile shows it in the match's case split: for every branch, core::check::substitute_in reads back and re-evaluates every value in the context, including the 160,000-element list. Core/kernel code: Opus lane, with a design note if the change is more than local.

D2264 (Matt, 3 Nov): start now.

Done 20f98102 (Opus, 75 min, est. 60), reviewed by the orchestrator (Opus), merged. The cost was in the elaborator case splits calling core substitute_in, not the kernel itself. New Unchanged checker (check.rs): a context value is kept as it is when x does not occur in it, every variable carries the Apart facts the identity environment would give, and it has none of: metas, folded defs, quot forms, glued calls with gluing off, closures, NatAdd, Nat Zero/Succ ctors, resumptions, erased fields; else the old path. Soundness needs only the first condition; the rest keep values identical (hashes and terms unchanged; checked by a temporary old-vs-new comparison on every example and std). Shared sequences visited once, keyed by address (all borrowed and immutable for the call). Reproducer (Parse.next on 160k chars): 6.67M -> 0.17M steps, 391-399 MB -> 93 MB. Display difference: inside a branch, a hypothesis holding a glued call that steps at once shows as the call rather than its whole result (as outside the branch); orchestrator call, kept (it is the saving; terms and hashes unchanged). Tests: core 356 (incl. fuzz daily sample), hash_stability 7, cli examples 9; orchestrator reran core + prelude hash, 357.

tickets.title: Parallel checking (deprioritised, D2299): measured ceiling 5.9x cold on aoc, ~3.4x with processes at 1.6-2.7x CPU, no gain for a typical edit
tickets.body:
Parallel checking: deprioritised (D2299, Matt, 4 Nov 2026). Measured in SW-1170; full write-up and scripts in dev/measurements/parallel-checking.md and dev/parallel-check/.

Findings (aoc unless noted; work from measured CPU, wall times under load 30+):
- Cold full check: 67.4 s of work, 11.5 s critical path, so the ceiling is 5.9x (reached at 8 cores). The critical path is two Proofs namespaces of ~8 s; one is mostly a single 6.4 s declaration group. Beyond ~6x needs parallelism inside a namespace.
- One process per namespace (model): ~3.4x (67 s -> 20 s); per day group ~4.0x (17 s). Costs 1.6-2.7x the CPU: each process spends 0.3-0.45 s re-elaborating the core, parsing the project and replaying a median of 30 library files from the cache (112 s CPU over 266 jobs).
- Prototype, 8 processes, library cached: CPU 156-160 s vs 153 s predicted; wall 29.7 s vs 73-108 s sequential (loaded machine, no quiet run).
- Typical edit: no gain (one Proofs/Tests namespace re-checked); a day's code namespace 0.56x (slower); Aoc.Common (59 namespaces) ~1.7x.
- Memory: a worker 130-190 MB after replay, heavy namespaces 0.8-1.3 GB (Day06.Proofs 1.25 GB); 8 workers summed 4.1 GB vs 1.6 GB sequential.
- games/rogue: ceiling 1.76x, processes at most 1.15x. Standard library alone: ceiling 2.2x (deep file chain).
- In-process threads on a frozen shared base (reasoning only): near 5.9x at sequential CPU, but need Rc -> Arc for core terms and Send elaborator state; same critical-path ceiling.

Why deprioritised: cold checks mostly happen in lanes and test tiers on an already saturated machine, where 2.5x the CPU mostly takes cores from other work, and the edit loop doesn't gain.

If revisited: cheapest first step is `check --jobs N` in the driver, one child process per day group along the import graph after the library is checked once, sharing the check cache; est. ~4x cold on a quiet machine, a day or two, no elaborator changes. The Globals split (D2290) keeps the in-process route open.

Related, better value for the edit loop: SW-1193 (warm check replays untouched namespaces, 3.8 s vs 0.5-1.7 s), SW-1194 (0.3 s CPU per process start), SW-1195 (six Proofs namespaces are 59% of a cold check).

Closed 4 Nov 2026 (backlog review): the measurement is the deliverable (merged 10d98d97d; dev/measurements/parallel-checking.md). Matt deprioritised it (D2299). Follow-ups: SW-1193 (done), SW-1194, SW-1195; the `check --jobs N` idea is noted on SW-1194.

tickets.title: fuzz_elab: kernel rejects an elaborated term from a mutated match.sw (full tier)
tickets.body:
Full tier at 1cef1def (SW-1175): fuzz_elab mutated_examples_check_without_internal_errors failed. Oracle 3 (kernel rejected an elaborated term): case 1050, seed 0x5eede1ab00000685, rng state 0xe3a9eaefcf2cbaaa, from accept/match.sw: E-TYPE-MISMATCH. Input saved (copy outside target/) in the orchestrator's scratchpad as 5eede1ab00000685-1050.sw. Find whether this is new tonight (elaborator-state steps 6a-7, SW-1179) or older, minimise, and fix the elaborator so it reports an error or builds a well-typed term. Expected: 60 min.

Progress (Opus, 04:59-05:20): commit 6b93dea2 on lane/SW-1182. Cause: equation generation, not the elaborator proper. `lenZero` in accept/match.sw (`match h: xs.length with | Zero => Yes rfl`) lifts to a helper whose result type mentions the matched column, so branch equations `lenZero.eq.zero/.succ` were stated ill-typed; the kernel refused them (E-REFL, E-TYPE-MISMATCH) and one_equation swallowed that as a skip ("the kernel refused the generated proof"). It happens on the unmutated example too; oracle 3 fired because it matches by message and the mutation added user E-TYPE-MISMATCH errors with the same "type mismatch" message. Not tonight's work: 8cffe0be (before SW-1152) refuses the same two terms. Fix: helper_call skips a match whose helper's result type mentions what it matches, with a reason. Test: function_equations a_generalising_matchs_branches_are_skipped_not_refused. Ran: function_equations + function_induct binaries (14 pass); fuzz_elab with FUZZ_CASES=1051 once (pass, 84 s). Follow-up: oracle 3 matches by message alone, so any swallowed kernel refusal plus an unrelated user error with the same message fails it.


Cause: lenZero in examples/accept/match.sw (a match h: whose helper result type mentions the scrutinee) had ill-typed branch equations the kernel refused silently; the mutation added a user E-TYPE-MISMATCH with the same message, which oracle 3 matched. Pre-existing (reproduced at 8cffe0be). Fix: skip such equations with a reason.
Model result: Opus, worked, 21 min (est. 60)

tickets.title: bench repeat: a second run in one process allocates once less on abilities-edge.sw (full tier)
tickets.body:
Full tier at 1cef1def (SW-1175): stitchwort-bench repeat counts_repeat_within_a_process failed: run 2 differed from run 1 by one allocation (4618791826 vs 4618791825; peak bytes 230708565 vs 230708541), all in accept/abilities-edge.sw (1598106 vs 1598105). Something carries state between two runs in one process. Suspects: tonight's state work (Logged shrink after rewind, SW-1179; Caches; Arc-shared session maps, 6b). Find it and make runs deterministic (or fix the cause), not loosen the test. Expected: 60 min.

Progress (lane, 4 Nov 05:00-05:10): reproduced with abilities-edge.sw alone, checked twice in one process (1598116 then 1598115). Logging allocation sizes in the counting allocator and diffing the two runs found one extra 24-byte allocation in run 1; its backtrace: Session::run_selected -> Cache::put -> Cache::key -> build_fingerprint's OnceLock<String> (filled on first use since SW-1136, 5e60fd18, 3 Nov). Not tonight's elaborator-state work. abilities-edge.sw is just the first file of the sweep. Cause: Cache::put built the key before checking which cache it was, so even Cache::disabled() formatted a key per test. Fix (bb7d65fb): only the memory cache builds the key. After the fix both runs match (1597530 each, about 586 fewer allocations per run for this file), and so do 11 other example files, each checked first in its own process. Tests: driver memory_cache unit tests (2 ok), bench repeat fast tier (ok, 4 s), clippy on driver clean.

Model result: Opus, worked, 9 min (est. 60)

tickets.title: Std: reconsider List.rangeFrom's argument order: `List.rangeFrom count start` reads backwards (day 3's `List.rangeFrom map.height 1` is 1, 2, … map.height steps). tickets.title: Design note: Scala-style partial-function lambdas (collect) in Stitchwort
tickets.body:
D2368 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): a match whose result is Option does NOT silently default missing cases to None; keep the exhaustiveness check, be explicit. But Matt wants Scala's partial-function vibe ('map with a partial function based on your match, emit things that don't match ... very high expressivity'): xs.collect { case ... => ... }. Orchestrator's sketch: (1) clause lambdas, a lambda written as match arms; (2) an explicitly marked partial form that desugars to a match whose arms are wrapped in Some with a final _ => None, so it fits List.filterMap / a new List.collect (a → Option b); partiality is opt-in and visible, so the exhaustiveness check stays everywhere else. Questions for the note: syntax (fits lambda-syntax.md's grammar, the | ambiguity in one-line matches), how it reads in pipelines, Option vs a dedicated PartialFn with isDefinedAt, guards, other uses (Map.collect, Parse alternatives, orElse chaining), what proofs see (it is an ordinary match; collect membership lemma), and survey of AoC sites that would use it.
Progress (lane, 4 Nov 22:18): note written, docs/proposals/partial-lambdas.md (commit 3665220a1 on lane/SW-1292). Recommends design B: `match | …` clause lambdas (total), `match? | …` (arms wrapped in Some, rest None; for filterMap/findMap), `matches | …` (Boolean side, Scala's cond; rest False, body-less arm = True); guards `| p if c => e` as a later stage. Rejects C (partial by callee type) and D (PartialFn record). Decisions P1-P10 for Matt. Survey: 10 pipeline sites (5 need guards), 10 Option tables, 12 total clause lambdas, Boolean form 6 aoc + 13 std.

Merged as a proposal; awaiting Matt's decisions P1–P10 (asked as D2370: accept the recommendations?). Model result: Opus, worked, 11 min (+ the cond addition) (est. 60).

D2370 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): 'I really like this.' Spelling: match | … (total clause lambda), match some | … (Some for listed cases, None otherwise), matches | … (true for listed cases, false otherwise); replaces the note's match?. Other recommendations accepted; guards (P3) being discussed as D2371.

tickets.title: Pattern guards (| p if c => e) in every match; follows SW-1294
tickets.body:
D2371 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): yes, as a follow-on stage after SW-1294. Stage 4 of docs/proposals/partial-lambdas.md (§6): | p if c => e in match … with, definition arms, and the three new forms (match, match some, matches). When the guard is false the arms below are tried; a guarded arm covers nothing for exhaustiveness (E-NONEXHAUSTIVE), so ordinary matches still need an unguarded arm, while match some / matches' hidden default covers the rest. Compiles to an if in the case tree whose else continues with the remaining arms; W-REDUNDANT with guarded arms; proofs see an ordinary if. Revives SW-237 (pruned without a note). Plan: Opus checks the design (a short note revising SW-237), then Sonnet implements; then migrate the five guarded pipeline sites (2024 days 6, 15, 20; 2021 day 18). Est. 3-4 h. Starts after SW-1294 merges.

Design note docs/proposals/pattern-guards.md (Opus, 15 min). Orchestrator's calls (minor, per Matt's overnight rule): (1) ship guards before generated equations exist (arms from the first guarded one get no equations/f.induct, E-NO-EQUATION with the reason); equations in a separate Opus lane; (2) migrate only 2024 day 15 positionsOf and 2021 day 18 orderedPairs (the others read better as filter/map); (3) guards may not perform operations (E-ABILITY), can be relaxed later. Implementation: Sonnet, same branch, est. 3-4 h.

Implemented (Sonnet, ~50 min, est. 210). Departure from the note: the kernel allows case only at the top of a body or branch, so the compiler makes the splits later rows need above the guard; the else tree holds only guards, leaves and missing cases. New E-GUARD-ARMS (absurd arm below a guard), E-MATCH-SIZE. AoC: 2024 d15 positionsOf, 2021 d18 orderedPairs. Opus review started 00:45 (generates kernel terms); day 18's audit went 15 -> 16 vacuity warnings, to explain. Findings: note §3.2 to correct; 'b != 0 && c != 0' gives no b ≠ 0 fact in an if (possible SW-226 gap).

Opus review (01:05): arm selection right on every input tried (columns, nested, literals, Vec/Fin, captures). Blocking: E-MALFORMED in the kernel when an arm below a guard is itself a match (in_tree not switched off for the else's leaves). Fix before merge: indexed-family matches falsely non-exhaustive after a guard; false E-GUARD-ARMS for nested (). Also: size limit too low for linear shapes; a misleading E-NO-EQUATION hint; note §3.2/§4 corrections. Sent back to the Sonnet lane (est. 60 min). Conjunction facts filed as SW-1305.

Review fixes done (7decb219e, d04608994): match bodies below a guard lifted; indexed missing cases tried with empty_case (and an impossible branch's guarded arms still type-checked); unit pattern below a guard; E-MATCH-SIZE 4096; hint and note corrections. Opus re-review of 7decb219e: nothing blocking, one fix (unchecked arm in an impossible branch), done in d04608994 (checks the chain first, then uses the empty-type term; reviewed by the orchestrator, not re-reviewed by Opus). Model result: Sonnet, needed fixes (kernel E-MALFORMED below a guard; indexed exhaustiveness; nested unit; an unchecked arm in an impossible branch, all found by the Opus review), ~100 min (est. 210).

tickets.title: if p && q (and auto generally) doesn't give each conjunct: 'if b != 0 && c != 0 then a % b' is E-AUTO-STUCK
tickets.body:
Found in the SW-1295 review, confirmed on main: neither an if on a conjunction nor auto splits p ∧ q into its parts, so 'if b != 0 && c != 0 then a % b else 0' fails with E-AUTO-STUCK (can't decide b ≠ 0); also with ∧, ≠ and b > 0 && c > 0. SW-226 only promised the right side of && knows the left. Applies to guards too ('| x if p && q =>'). Likely small in auto: split conjunction hypotheses.

DeepSeek attempt (branch ds/SW-1305, 18c225a1b; ~60 min) works on the examples but not merged: beyond its brief it changed how every 'if b && c' on propositions elaborates (both branches elaborated twice, the conjunction form kept only if a branch's auto proof uses it; doubling cost for nested ifs) and refactored unused_proof_if, which conflicts with SW-1295's check_if. Orchestrator's call: rerun on Opus, using the attempt as a reference. Model result: DeepSeek, failed (went past the brief's limit into a general change to if; design-level), 60 min (est. 60).

Opus lane (lane/SW-1305, f98bc2c74; started 02:01, done ~02:36, est. 90 min). The Bool reading of `a && b` records on the way the conjunction its operands decide (decided props, or a Bool c as c = True; at least one prop; b not using a's proof) with decision `Decidable.andThen da (_ => db)` (new std def, short-circuits like &&). `if` on it goes through the decided path like `if b != 0`; unused proof → the recorded Bool reading, so terms unchanged (prelude snapshot: only the two new defs added). One elaboration of the condition and branches. auto: parts of conjunction hypotheses (And.left/right, 8 deep) as a last step. Checks: elab lane, examples+hashes for auto-conjunction/pattern-guard, binary(hash_stability), std self-tests, aoc + rogue check: all pass. Bench: the check-number-*/text-literal/nested-parens "regressions" are identical on main without the change (stale baseline). Not covered: `if n != 0 && len % n == 0 then len / n` (b uses a's proof; needs a dependent conjunction), proof-valued ifs (check_proof_if keeps the Bool form).

Done on Opus (f98bc2c74, 35 min, est. 90): logic::condition records a ∧ b and a decision (new std Decidable.andThen/andYes) while reading a && b as Bool; check_if_in then takes the same path as 'if b != 0' (unused proof falls back to the original Bool term, so no hash moves; prelude snapshot gains the two new functions); auto tries conjunction parts last, depth 8. Guards benefit. Not covered: 'if n != 0 && len % n == 0' (dependent conjunction). Orchestrator's calls (minor): a Bool operand reads as c = True inside a conjunction, keep; the two std functions, yes. Bench drift is the stale 2 Nov baseline (identical with the change stashed).

Merged 2f7bf899b; verified: merge tier 1078/1078, hashes, fmt, natives, std_library, guide, aoc check and 1364 tests, rogue, audit. Model result: Opus, worked, 35 min (est. 90).

tickets.title: Research and design note: non-empty lists in std (NonEmpty with reduce, head, last, maximum without Option), as Idris, Lean, Agda and Haskell do it; where the code base would model its data better with it
tickets.body:
D2383 (Matt, 5 Nov): 'let's file tickets to look at how we might do non-empty lists in the standard library so that we can have things like reduce, probably lots of other useful things. I'd be interested to see what our options are for this, what other languages like Idris, Lean, Agda [do]. What opportunities there might be in the existing code base to use it to better model the data. I think, in a way, having more precise types is powerful.' Options to compare: a record { head, tail }, a List with a proof (xs ≠ [] as a refinement / subtype), an indexed Vec (n+1), Haskell's NonEmpty; conversions, pattern syntax ([x, ..xs] for both?), how parsers (many1, sepBy1, lines, sections) would return it, how proofs use it. Survey std (maximum, minimum, last, head?) and aoc/rogue for Option-returning or partial uses that a non-empty type would remove. Opus.

D2403 (Matt, 5 Nov): yes, an Opus lane; 'definitely do a thorough search of existing languages to see what other people do, including Swift, Rust, Kotlin, etc.' Prompted by List.range (Int.toNat target.right). Constraint: .. already means spread in brackets ([x, ..rest]), so Haskell's [2..n] would clash. Cover inclusive/exclusive, Nat/Int/Char, steps and counting down, List vs lazy, membership lemma (x ∈ a ..< b ↔ a ≤ x < b, pairs with chained comparisons), patterns, Fin, loops, and the List.range argument-order question (SW-1258). Opus, ~45 min. Next free slot.

Done on lane/SW-1356 (30797b999): docs/proposals/ranges.md. 25-language survey with sources; ~1,100 range sites (578 of aoc's 679 in proofs). Recommends a ..< b and a ..= b as List.range a b; no [a..b]. Decisions R1–R9 asked as D2405–D2413. Model result: Opus, worked, 8 min (est. 45).

Matt, 5 Nov 2026: 'I approve the range syntax of Stitchwort. Please cue that for implementation.' D2405-D2413 all as recommended: a ..< b and a ..= b, no bare .. or [a..b] (error names both) (D2405); both forms, ..= b is ..< b + 1 (D2406); a range is a List, the call List.range a b (D2407); List.range (from) (until) replaces one-arg List.range and List.between, rangeFrom stays (D2408); Nat then Int by type, Char later (D2409); reversed is empty, .reverse to count down, no step syntax (D2410); Bool x in a ..< b decided by comparisons (D2411); no range patterns now (D2412); W-RANGE-IN-BRACKETS (D2413). Implementation: steps 1-5 of docs/proposals/ranges.md §13, one after another.

tickets.body:
From SW-1748, 7 Nov 2026. Determinism risk; stage 6b should know.

SW-1784: pre-existing, not caused by stage 1b. Likely cause (from the code, not reproduced): a call caches its unfolding without recording whether gluing was on; forced unglued (decide, instrumentation), a later folded read-back can write that full unfolding. tickets.body:
From Overmind soak report 1 (Matt's laptop, NixOS i7-6700HQ 8 threads, 15 GiB; 7 Nov, commit a3c652a63). Mutated from reject/reads-weaken-over-map-implicits, accept/reads-done-spec-from-expected, reads-named-parser, int-literals-auto, reads-nested-binds, reject/parser-count-differs-from-lemma, accept/pure-fold-in-parse-function. The laptop took 2,402 s, 7x slower, against 2x on the AoC check. So likely slow there, not hangs. Suspect: the laptop's binary is the musl target, whose allocator is slow under threads. First step: on the laptop, time one of the 7 saved inputs with a glibc build against the musl one.

Sharper suspect: the CLI sets mimalloc as its global allocator (crates/cli/src/main.rs:515), so the AoC check (2x slower on the laptop) uses it; the fuzzer is a test binary (crates/driver/tests/fuzz_elab.rs) with no global allocator, so on Linux it uses musl's malloc (flake.nix builds for musl), which is slow with many threads (7x slower). Matt is asking Overmind to compare 200 cases with and without mimalloc in the test binary.

Confirmed on Overmind (ad49343d0), 200 cases, same seed: default allocator 229.5 s and 225.3 s (warm), mimalloc in the test binary 37.5 s, same work (identical rates). About 6x: musl's allocator in test binaries. None of the 200 hit 60 s even on the default allocator; cases 558, 737, 1619 not reached. Fix: SW-2109. Then rerun the 2,000 on Overmind to settle the 7.

SW-2109 merged. Remaining: rerun 2,000 cases on Overmind with mimalloc to settle cases 558, 737, 1619.

About 1 batch in 1000. Profile and fix (elaborator or kernel)
tickets.body:
From SW-2570. Repro: STITCHWORT_EFFECT_FUZZ_SEED=1794200310 STITCHWORT_EFFECT_FUZZ_BATCHES=1 cargo test --release -p stitchwort-cli --test extraction effect_differential::generated -- --nocapture (dump the module). Possibly exponential evaluation of open Nat terms. Profile first. 120 min.

Started 10 Nov 00:55 (est. 120 min), on lane/SW-2572 (Opus).

10 Nov 01:45, to review. Profile (macOS `sample`, seed 1794200310 shrunk to `let a := if (x + 500000) % 2 == 0 then 4 else 4; if a % 2 == 0 ...`): all the time in `native::as_nat_with` forcing already-unfolded calls under the elaborator's obligations loop. Cause: `(x + k) % 2` multiplies a quotient of k/2 `Succ`s around a stuck step by 2; `*` peels one `Succ` a step, and at each step `native::run` walked the rest of the chain to see it wasn't a number: quadratic in k. Not exponential, not let sharing. Fix (core, `native.rs`, so the kernel computes this way too; docs/core.md updated; needs an Opus review per D2364): `Nat.mul`'s shortcut for unknowns, `(k + m) * n = k*n + m * n` for a number n, in one step; and `native::run` checks every number argument's head before walking a `Succ` chain, so `(k + m) * y` with y unknown is linear too. What's equal is unchanged. Timings (user s): `(x + 16000) % 2` 10.1 -> 0.46, `((x+16000)/2)*y` 9.2 -> 0.56; seed 1794200310's module >10 min -> 4.3 s; the other four seeds 1.0-1.5 s; 200 fuzzer batches from 1794200000 in 51 s, none skipped. Tests: new `resources::remainders_of_long_numbers_check_in_linear_time` (1.5 s), Mul added to `natives::shortcuts_with_unknowns_agree_with_the_definitions` (a mutated shortcut fails it), `a_batch_the_checker_cannot_finish_stops_at_the_deadline` deadline 5 s -> 1 s (the seed now checks in about 4 s). Lanes core, elab, effects, hashes pass. Left: `Nat.divFuel` still builds a quotient one `Succ` a step (linear, ~13 us per unit: `(x + 500000) % 2` forced fully takes 7 s); a divFuel shortcut would be a new kernel shortcut, proposed as a follow-up.

Done 10 Nov. Cause: (x + k) % 2's quotient is k/2 Succs around a stuck division; Nat.mul peeled one per step and native::run re-walked the chain each time (quadratic). Fix (native.rs, kernel): (k + m) * n -> k·n + m * n in one step when m starts with a Succ; head checks before Succ walks. Opus review: sound, F1-F4 fixed (docs/reviews/SW-2572-nat-mul-shortcut-review.md). Seed 1794200310 > 10 min -> 4.3 s; 200 batches 51 s, none skipped. Follow-ups SW-2603 (divFuel), SW-2604 (budget for Succ walks), SW-2605 (deadline test input). Model result: Opus, worked, 47 + 20 + 15 min (est. 120).

tickets.title: Kernel: a data type becomes final with an index type that mentions a failed declaration
tickets.body:
Severity 3 (missing guard), from SW-2659 (docs/reviews/SW-2659-kernel-soundness-audit.md, F2).

declare_indexed_data_group lets a failed reference through in the parameters and index types ('define_data_group finds it again', crates/core/src/check.rs:2815, 2832). admit_data_group re-checks the parameters, fields and result indices (check.rs:3087, 3113, 3223) but not the members' index telescopes. So a group whose index type mentions a failed definition, with fields and result indices that don't, becomes final, against admissible's invariant (check.rs:3483) and docs/core.md ('nothing built on it is ever accepted').

No path to False found: the failed definition is a neutral constant and anything mentioning it directly is still refused. No CLI repro (the surface can't write it).

Fix: in admit_data_group, pass every member's index types to the first admissible call. A core test: a failed definition in an index type, no constructors, must fail with E-FAILED-DEPENDENCY.


Progress (10 Nov, Opus lane, 943deae32): guard added in admit_data_group (every member's index types join the first admissible call). Test admission::an_index_type_that_uses_a_failed_declaration_fails_the_type (fails without the guard: "ok"). docs/core.md admission rule now names index types and result indices.

tickets.title: Kernel: a data type's parameter types aren't checked for case outside a case tree
tickets.body:
Severity 3 (missing guard), from SW-2659 (docs/reviews/SW-2659-kernel-soundness-audit.md, F3).

Signatures, fields, indices and result indices all go through case_only_in_tree(ty, false) (crates/core/src/check.rs:2303, 3105, 2836, 3228). A data group's parameter types don't, in declare_indexed_data_group (check.rs:2815-2821) or admit_trusted_data_decls (check.rs:3378-3403). check accepts a Case wherever it is checked against a type (a lambda body in an argument: check.rs:438, 541), and a case outside a definition's tree that gets stuck panics (crates/core/src/value.rs:2482).

Only a wrong elaborator or cache entry reaches it; the result is a panic, not a false theorem.

Fix: the same check on each parameter type in both functions, with a core test.


Progress (10 Nov, Opus lane with SW-2674, 943deae32): case_only_in_tree on each parameter type in declare_indexed_data_group and admit_trusted_data_decls. Test admission::a_parameter_type_cannot_hold_a_case covers both paths (without the guard it panics at value.rs:2482).

- Promise: `Promise::ProofsOnly` (`sweep theorem-binders --proofs-only`, `trial-edits --proofs-only`). In a recursive group, proof-result members stand apart (else a theorem's lifted `%match` moved it). JS and the runtime drop exactly these (JS: `Quot.lift` is `f q`, `J` its base). Content hashes unchanged (std/aoc/rogue lists identical to SW-2690's).

tickets.title: rewrite h in rfl with h: Nat.equal m n = True on (if m = n then 1 else 0) = 1 fails with E-CANNOT-INFER, on main before and after SW-2812: bug in carrying through Nat.decEq or in the message
tickets.body:
Found by SW-2812. Repro:
```
import Std (Bool, Eq, Nat)

theorem c (m: Nat) (n: Nat) (h: Nat.equal m n = True): (if m = n then 1 else 0) = 1 :=
  rewrite h in rfl
```

Progress (11 Nov, Opus lane): cause found and fixed. The usual motive fails (the decision's `sound` is typed by `Nat.equal m n = True`), so rewrite carries `Nat.decEq`'s proofs along the equation (carry.rs). Its proofs are lambdas (`h => Nat.equalSound m n h`), and carrying built the redexes `(h => S) e` and `(h => C) h'`; the kernel can't infer a lambda's type, so checking the motive failed with the kernel's E-CANNOT-INFER. Only decisions whose proofs are calls (as in rewrite-decision-plain-first) worked. Fix in `Carry::carried`: a lambda `sound` takes the carried proof through a `let` typed `s = True`; a lambda `complete` takes its argument, a variable, by substitution. Example examples/accept/rewrite-decision-lambda-proofs.sw with its hash snapshot. Tests: the repro checks; EXAMPLES=rewrite-decision-lambda-proofs,rewrite-decision running examples tests 3/3 pass; hash_stability::examples for the new example passes. Commit 8405657db.

Also: the stack error's wording ('nested too deeply for the conversion'; Depth would match same_spines). Review: docs/reviews/SW-2874-g2-nested-sums-review.md 3c, 4c, 7
tickets.body:
Estimate: 75 min (started 16:51, done 17:25).

Progress (Opus lane, 11 Nov 2026). Measured first, release CLI, `check --no-cache`, STITCHWORT_TIMINGS (elab ms / kernel ms / steps for the theorem). Probes: `repEnd n x e` (structural, `x + repEnd k x e`), equal (`repEnd D x y = repEnd (D-1) x (x + y)`) and unequal (`... y = ... z`); `decreasing` `f (Succ k) y = y + f k y`, equal (`x + f D y = x + (y + f (D-1) y)`) and unequal (`f D` against `f (D-1)`).

Before:
- rep equal 1,000: 88 / 83 ms, 129k steps. 10,000: 7,550 / 7,356 ms, 1.29M steps, 15.3 s wall. Profile: `reread_with` (unifier and kernel). Quadratic and uncounted, as the review said.
- dec equal 10,000: 268 / 301 ms, 13.5M steps (fine). dec unequal 10,000: 33,219 ms elab, 14.8M steps, 33.7 s; profile again `reread_with` in the unifier.
- rep unequal 1,000: 3,443 ms, 90M steps; 10,000 > 60 s. Not reread: the profile is `refl_error` -> `Ctx::show` evaluating for the message (finding, below).

Change: `nat_add::reread` is a loop (no Rust recursion, so no `nesting("conversion")` and no profile-dependent E-RESOURCE from it; review 4c and 7 gone), charges `budget.step()` per sum it goes down to (not the top one), and takes an `Unread` record: the sums a walk found nothing to unfold in, by spine address (values kept). A later walk stops at one. Kept per outermost `conv` (in its `CallMemo`) and per outermost unification (in the unifier's `CallMemo`, valid while `effects` — epoch, trail length, postponed — is unchanged); `case`s and the reference evaluator pass a fresh one. Off with the shortcuts off. docs/core.md rule E says so.

After:
- rep equal 1,000: 4 / 3 ms, 133k steps. 10,000: 86 / 34 ms, 1.33M steps, 0.36 s wall (was 15.3 s).

New test `nested_sum_walks_a_plain_chain_once` (depth 400: 75k steps; 393k and 15 s with the record switched off, checked). Depth 1,000 runs out of stack in the test thread, in conv comparing the sums' arguments (opens-by-tree path, per level), not in reread.
