Findings: (1) a failed `rfl` on long stuck-sum chains renders its message with quadratic-or-worse evaluation (rep unequal 1,000: 90M steps, 3.4 s; 10,000 > 60 s), `check::refl_error` -> `Ctx::show`. (2) conv of two `Nat.add` chains recurses on the Rust stack per level (opens-by-tree argument compare), so depth ~1,000 is E-RESOURCE in a test thread.

Review follow-ups (Fable review docs/reviews/SW-2875-g2-walk-once-review.md, 11 Nov 2026):
- 4b, what made the `decreasing` unequal probe faster: the record, measured. Same build with the record switched off (a temporary env switch, since removed): dec unequal 10,000 took 23,728 ms and 214.8M steps (24.2 s); with it, 614 ms and 15.0M steps. rep equal 10,000 off: 9,145 / 9,204 ms, 201.3M steps; on: 42 / 30 ms, 1.33M. The review's reading (each walk of a chain built by unfolding unfolds something, so nothing is filed) holds only for the first walks. Traced at depth 1,000: 17 walks unfolded something (8,005 sums between them); the other 3,602 unfolded nothing and were filed (7,818 sums). Without the record, 7,918 such walks went over 2.0M sums. Most likely why (reasoned, not traced): the `decreasing` calls are glued calls that keep their unfoldings, and `view_with` forces them, so once the first walks have unfolded the chain, later walks see the plain sums under them and unfold nothing. So "34 s to 1.1 s" stands, from the record; the step charge and the loop add steps and don't save time.

tickets.body:
Lane notes (Opus, 12 Nov 2026, 17:08-17:35, est. 2 h):

- **M2** (205b825bb): the reader evaluates with calls kept folded and, with gluing off, starts from the fact's type as written (variable's declared type, annotation, argument's parameter type, the definition's own type, match columns). Glued: unchanged (early return). Test: `elaboration readings::a_user_reading_is_found_{glued,unglued}`. Gap: an expected test fact with no written type to hand (e.g. a lambda body's expected type) still reads the unfolded value unglued.
- **L1** (8e7030550): `ItemInfo.reading` holds each `@[reading]` theorem's test function and polarity from its syntax; a use above it stops at the function with E-NO-READING "`inRange`'s reading, `inRangeReads`, is declared below" + label at the reading. A reading whose proof fails is filed as its D3527 stand-in, so users rely on it ("2 declarations rely on a declaration with an error"); with no stand-in, E-FAILED-DEPENDENCY (dropped beside the reading's own error). Examples: reject/reading-declared-below.sw, reject/reading-failed.sw.
- **L2** (5d9e12514), orchestrator-level call taken by the lane: refuse. A reading whose test passes the function more arguments than its definition takes (`def tiny: Nat → Bool := small`) is E-READING-SHAPE, since `tiny n` unfolds to `small n` before anything reads it and the reading was dead. Filing under `small` was rejected: it breaks E-READING-PLACE when `small` is elsewhere. Example: reject/reading-alias.sw.
- Kernel terms: glued, unchanged (hash_stability passes). Unglued, the reader's proof terms now hold folded calls (`inRangeReads lo x hi`), as glued ones do.
- Tests: readings:: (2 pass), test:example NAME=reading (7 pass), projects reading tests (6 pass), hash_stability (10 pass), running examples accepted|goal|rejected|soundness (7 pass).


Review fixes (cfa9f87c7, 17:42-17:52):
- M3/L1 unglued: `as_written` uses the written type only where it is convertible to the fact's type (resource errors propagate: L3), and reads refined variables from the context (`let h2 := h; match x with …`). Placeholder arguments (check.rs) pass the head up to the argument (`head_before_placeholder`), so `t x {..} {..}` checks each argument against its own parameter.
- L2: pending readings matched by the name the statement resolves to (`Elaborator::named`), or a dot form's function name (`b.ok`); `Iff (…) (…)` recognised.
- M1: `readings::a_helper_above_the_reading_that_it_uses_checks`, ignored (fails today with "can't be built with `Both` yet"), ready for the checking-order decision.
- Tests: readings:: 4 pass + the ignored one fails as expected (--run-ignored all); test:example NAME=reading 7 pass; running examples accepted|goal|rejected|soundness 7 pass; clippy elab + elaboration test target clean.


D3537 (Matt, 12 Nov 2026: 'Happy to go with your recommendations'): dependency order, not file position, decides which uses see a reading: uses wait for the reading via an ordering edge; the reading's own dependencies read by unfolding; no 'declared below'.

D3537 built (d1b6626c3, 18:22-18:36, est. 60 min; merged main first, 3152411bd):
- `reading_edges` (module.rs, before `instance_edges`, not in the library): each `@[reading]` item's test function resolved from its syntax (`f`, `Ns.f`, `x.f` by last name, `↔` or `Iff`); every Def/Test item depending on it, and not reached by the reading, gets a speculative edge to the reading. No cycles by construction.
- The "declared below" E-NO-READING is gone; `examples/reject/reading-declared-below.sw` became `examples/accept/reading-used-above.sw` (+ hash snapshot). A failed reading with no stand-in still gives the quiet E-FAILED-DEPENDENCY.
- In the reading's dependencies, a failed read gets a note: "`inRange`'s reading, `inRangeReads`, isn't available here: `inRangeReads` depends on this declaration, so here `inRange` reads as what it unfolds to" (no_reading, E-NOT-A-RECORD, the dot field fallback; not in the reading's own proof).
- Tests: readings:: 8 pass (helper above reading un-ignored, use above, Iff and dot forms from above, the why-note, two-file order both ways); test:example NAME=reading 7; projects reading 6; hash_stability 10 (new snapshot); examples accepted|goal|rejected|soundness 7.

Fix (lane/SW-3017, f86367df1): check_attempt skips Elaborator::is_unfinished(id) (final and relying on no assumption, as audit reads it).

Fuzz with the fix, seed 0x2c02: VOID=20 534 attempts 0 findings; VOID=1500 2014 attempts (29 accepted) 0 findings, 68 s.
Tests: proofs stand_ins:: (1 pass); tools test_json::|audit:: (49 pass).

tickets.title: [Opus] Native JIT: n1::bodies_count_their_entries_when_asked panics in cranelift-jit X86PCRel4 relocation (compiled_blob.rs:172:80, PosOverflow) on Linux x86_64, deterministic since ba4e20071 (SW-3128's may_perform_at loop, crates/elab/src/effects.rs only); base 208510a37 passes (Overmind bisect). Two questions: why the effects analysis change alters what the JIT compiles (it was meant to give identical answers), and why a 32-bit PC-relative reference reaches a symbol >2 GiB away
tickets.body:
Lane (Opus, 13 Nov 2026, 16:57-17:10, est. 2 h): branch lane/SW-3139, commit ae340838a.

- Effects: ba4e20071 changes no answer. The old may_perform_at was run beside the new one and both answers and visit counts compared: 294,521 calls over the prelude (hash_stability::prelude), plus the n1 tests and the effect examples (about 14,000 more). No difference. So no effects fix: the bisect landed on a commit that only moved where things got mapped.
- Relocation: the X86PCRel4 is the `lea` for the body's name data (`{symbol}.name`, the count_bodies instrumentation: first_part's symbol_value). The data was declared Linkage::Local, so `colocated`, so PC-relative. cranelift-jit's SystemMemoryProvider mmaps code and data separately with no nearness guarantee (likely culprit for the distance: the tests' 16 GiB with_stack thread stack, with holes above and below it). Fix: n1::far_data marks the reference not colocated, so it is a movabs/Abs8 (x86-64) or literal load (aarch64). Calls between JIT functions are fine: cranelift-jit veneers out-of-range calls. Helpers are Import and already Abs8.
- Test: n1::tests::code_reads_data_mapped_far_away maps data 8 GiB from code; it panics in cranelift-jit with the data colocated (aarch64 adrp arm, compiled_blob.rs:324) and passes with the fix. bodies_count_their_entries_when_asked also asserts no `symbol colocated` in its listing.
- Needs Linux verification: n1::bodies_count_their_entries_when_asked and n1::tests::code_reads_data_mapped_far_away on Overmind.
Verified on Linux x86_64 by Overmind at 664e62326: both tests pass (the n1 test failed 20/20 before). Model result: Opus, worked (plus a libc dev-dependency fixup for Linux), 12 min (est. 120).

Make the build rebuild/check the runtime library with the CLI, or give a clear message naming task build (SW-3145 finding)
tickets.body:
Matt, 14 Nov 2026: tidy batch before the foundations ('built programs not starting is a pretty big bug'). SW-3234 found plain build fails too: 'this executable's program can't be read: written by a different build of the runtime'. Expected: 1.5 h (Sonnet).

Sonnet lane, 14 Nov 2026: root cause was that `cargo build -p stitchwort-cli` never rebuilds libstitchwort_standalone.a (a separate package; only `task build` or test builds made it), so after any core/syntax/rt change the CLI's build hash (rt/build.rs) differed from the library's, and every executable failed at start (plain and --native; --native on a no-native CLI is a separate clear error). Reproduced. Fix (d3d200a2f): the CLI depends on stitchwort-standalone (so every build makes a current library in deps/), the library embeds stitchwort_rt::BUILD_MARKER, and `build` picks a library holding the CLI's marker (env, beside exe, ../lib/stitchwort, deps/) and otherwise errors "different build ... task build". Test: a_stale_runtime_library_is_refused; existing build tests pass. Model result pending review.


Tidy batch (Matt, 14 Nov 2026). Expected: 1.5 h (Sonnet), ~9 min. Cause: crates/standalone was its own package, so cargo build -p stitchwort-cli never rebuilt it; its runtime-source hash then disagreed with the CLI's. Fix: a normal dependency, BUILD_MARKER in the library, find_library picks the matching one and names stale ones. Leftovers: Taskfile's -p stitchwort-standalone now redundant; old deps/ copies (~29 MB each) not cleaned. Model result: Sonnet, worked, 9 min (est. 90).

Progress (lane, 14 Nov 22:25): root cause: in recovery mode R1 (`ran_out`) lets an expression slot read no tokens, so a local `def`'s result type after `:` can be an empty token range; `local_def`'s "needs a body" error spanned it with `tokens_span`, which indexed `tokens[start]`, one past the last token at the end of the input (and the next line's token before a block-ending line, a wrong span). tickets.title: [Opus] Writing [t := Char] [b := List Nat] by hand on a readsThen breaks a proof that checks with neither or either alone: knowing every type early changes which arguments wait for the expected type (pre-existing; SW-3282 finding)
tickets.body:
Found in SW-3282; repro c3tb.sw in docs/reviews/SW-3282-settle-from-expected.md S3 (probes in the scratch sw3282-review folder). Fixing it unblocks SW-3307 (settle every type parameter). Expected: 2 h (Opus).

**Progress (lane, 15 Nov 2026, 02:16-03:15).** Done; commit 1b949c461 on `lane/SW-3304`.

- **Cause (traced):** not the review's guess. Written implicits keep a call off `propagation_plan` altogether (the written result mentions them), so with `[t := …]` or `[b := …]` every step goes through `fallback_inferred`: `readsNat` fails in place, the `rest` lambda is held, and `finish_application` compares the step's `Reads (() => bind (?p ()) ?j) ?spec` with the goal by `unify_solving_arguments`. The goal's parser is the outer step's `?j x0`, solved as `bind (nat ()) (x1 => …)`. `same_calls` only fires for two unforced `Value::Call`s, so a call against a *solved unknown* standing for a call of the same definition was unfolded on both sides, through `runFrom`'s handlers, until `?p ()` met `Parse.nat`'s `match` over the state: no solution. With `b` unknown it passed by accident: `?b`, solved at the `value` binder, made the `bind` call stale, `values_differ` re-read both sides, and the re-read put the solution back as a call.
- **Fix:** `unify_step` looks through a solved unknown at either head; two calls of one definition go to `same_calls`. Only while solving from arguments (without that limit day 2 +2.2%, Std.Parse +0.4%). Which arguments wait is unchanged.
- **Numbers** (`STITCHWORT_TIMINGS=decls check --no-cache`, summed per namespace, before -> after; nodes identical everywhere): day 2 proofs 6,890,500 -> 6,896,050 (+0.08%); day 7 6,609,827 -> 6,607,194 (-0.04%); day 18 2,236,096 unchanged; Std.Parse 99,478,662 -> 99,482,727 (+0.004%).
- **Tests:** new accept example `reads-chain-written-type-arguments` (all eight combinations of `t`/`a`/`b` written; two fail before) + hash snapshot; `binary(library) & test(/hash_stability|reads_chain_cost/)` 11/11, no other snapshot changed; elab `unify|propagat|implicit|settle` 43/43; examples `reads-chain,parse-row` and `unknown-solved,dictionary,from-expected,reads-` accept+reject pass; all 18 SW-3282 review probes and the reject examples give byte-identical output to the binary before the fix (c3tb now checks); `check --no-cache` of 2020 days 2, 7, 18 pass.
- **SW-3307 measurement (not committed):** dropping `settle_from_expected`'s row condition (so `b` is given too): day 2 proofs 6.90M -> 4.83M (-30%; `runsPieces` 6.17M -> 4.10M, about 24% under its pre-generic 5.41M), day 7 -9.1%, day 18 -0.9%, Std.Parse -1.4%. All three days check; all eight combos check. But nodes change (Std.Parse 702,774 -> 702,751; day 7 +12), so hashes move, and one reject example regresses: `reads-nested-binds-unknown-field` gives E-TYPE-MISMATCH at the final `rfl` (`?3 read value`) instead of E-UNKNOWN-FIELD at `first`. Errors also change in review probes g1, g2, g8, r1, t2 (unreviewed). `reads-chain-swapped-pair` differs only in a meta number.

D3618 (Matt, 15 Nov 2026): "I think my initial inclination is actually maybe we should be doing D. Maybe every comment can be placed. Otherwise, we have a sort of kind of partial function for our formatter where we can format almost everything except if you happen to have a comment in a weird place, in which case it gives up for part of the file. And if we discover that people are putting comments in weird places for good reasons, we can improve the formatting on a case by case basis". He was unsure about the token-ownership rule ("Maybe it's fine, but I don't really know"): not approved as such; the orchestrator treats it as an implementation choice, judged by the requirements (never give up; the comment stays beside the code it was next to; formatting twice changes nothing), and will show Matt real before/after output from the lanes.

Lane (Opus, 16 Nov, est. 60 min, ~25 min): one parse per case decided.
- row.sw: the parser was wrong. After an arrow ending its line, a `{e}` line at the block's own column continued the line (as docs say) but `peek` hid the `{` as a stop, so `result_type` missed the row and read `{e} a` as a record applied to `a`. - arms.sw: the parser was right (match alternatives at 15, a `|` at 6 is the definition's arm). The formatter joined a block type to the `:` when there are no parameters. Fixed: a block type starts below the `:`; fmt test a_result_type_that_is_a_block_starts_below_its_colon.
- D candidate (not implemented): a type is never a block. A `let`'s type and a `match` scrutinee already read lines at one column as one expression (expr_inline); a definition's result type and a parameter's type read them as a block, so `def names:\n  List\n  Text` is `List; Text`. tickets.body:
Paper lane (Fable), 17 Nov 2026, about 15 min (est. 60). Note: docs/proposals/derived-instances-rethink.md.

Findings (all measured with the release CLI at 0d09b858a, synthetic types):
- The cost is cubic in fields per constructor, linear in constructors. One constructor: 4 fields 0.28M steps, 8 fields 2.0M, 16 fields 19.3M (1.6 s), 32 fields 233M (30 s). SW-3710's "50K per constructor per proof" is the two-field case.
- Causes isolated: (a) reading field k's equation as And.left (And.right^k q) is cubic (1.15M steps at 16 fields; 75K with tails let-bound; the J chain itself 9K); (b) an elaborator slow path: a 32-term chain of (DecEq.decide a b).holds && ... is 1.54M steps where a == b && ... is 54K; (c) the decision and the congruence are stated two or three times.
- A prototype of == through nested pairs (Pair.decMk + one Eq.cong) checks and is 3x cheaper at 4 fields, 13x at 16, 26x at 32.
- Warm check cache: Nat importer 1.95 s cold, 0.34 s warm, 0.28 s with no import.
- Field types matter little (derived field 1.4x, not 3x); instances in scope don't matter.

Recommendation: C (fix the elaborator path, reshape proofs, step-budget test) and D (per-user std cache, reopening D281); neither A nor B. Two questions for Matt at the note's end.

Model result: fable, worked, 15 min (est. 60). Recommends C + D, not A/B. Filed SW-3726 SW-3727.

tickets.body:
Lane notes (Opus, 17 Nov 2026, 15:13-15:45; est. 55 min):

tickets.body:
Lane notes (Opus, 19 Nov 2026, branch lane/SW-4091, commit 4e6e65670; 18:16-18:46, about 30 min, est. 75). Covers SW-4113 too.

- Cause: a proof step that only carries a hypothesis whose calls compute to more than 2 million nodes (`big: q (grow 22 (Leaf x))`) read that hypothesis back in full: the rewrite's kernel context (quote_folded forces calls that step at once), a generalised match's occurrence test (every hypothesis unfolded; one too large abandoned the usual generalisation, and the unknowns scan's folded fallback was too large too, unlabelled, so the error pointed at the whole theorem). A tuple let on a lemma's proof of ∧ or ∃ in a proof is such a match (SW-4113's shape; SW-4091's ∃ inside a mutual block likely the same). Printing an open goal with such a hypothesis had no limit at all: 24 GB with grow 30.
- Fix (elaborator and printer only; the kernel's read-back is unchanged): check::quote_folded falls back to the read-back as written (convertible) when the folded one is too large (Ctx::quote_folded, lift, goal snapshots); a generalised match reads each hypothesis's type as written when the unfolded one is too large (may leave it unrefined; motive checked as before), and its scan error points at the match; pretty's shown read-back is capped at 2M nodes, then as written.
- Tests (each fails before, passes after, with the parent's code built and run): examples/accept/large-hypothesis-carried.sw (rewrite at another hypothesis, let-pair on ∧, let-pair on ∃, match on an expression: 4 E-RESOURCE at the whole theorem before), examples/accept/large-hypothesis-match.sw (the old reject example's hypothesis form), examples/goals/large-hypothesis-goal.sw (E-RESOURCE before). Snapshots: goal, 2 hash, reject rewrite-value-too-large (its note now names the too-large call, as its comment says), reject as-written-unconfirmed-slow-check (now with the call in the goal, which still runs out with the number note).
- Ran: test:example on those plus 7 related too-large examples; resources tests (5 too-large/match ones); tools check_early (3); hash_stability for the new examples and prelude (std hashes unchanged).
- Left: a step whose own target is too large (`rewrite same at big`) still runs out, pointing at the step; proving guide gives the transport-lemma workaround. Not checked against the original tools/fmt proofs (whole-project check is not a lane's).


Follow-up (Opus, 19 Nov 18:52-19:03): the two resources failures (running_out_of_steps_names_the_definition_being_unfolded, a_long_check_says_what_it_is_computing_while_it_runs) are not from SW-4091: both fail with core+elab at the merge's parent, at this lane's base c56c7005a, and before SW-4218 and SW-4032. [Opus] Rest-lambda continuations: the 5 [j :=][k :=] pairs SW-4330 left (Statements, DeclData, DeclHeaders x2, FormsBlocks) fail because the rest lambda's body is checked against Follows unfolded through runFrom before ?j is known; hold the lambda until after the as-written comparison, or compare on the call (elaborator ordering)
tickets.body:
Estimate: 60 min (Opus lane, 20 Nov 2026).

Progress (lane, 20 Nov):
- 3 of the 5 pairs (FollowsStatements followsStatementOther, FollowsDeclData followsDeclarationRefusal, FollowsDeclHeaders followsHeaderGroupColon) already elaborate on main without the pair: dropped, commit 8aa2a11c6 on lane/SW-4355. No elaborator change.
- The other 2 (FollowsDeclHeaders followsRowStart, FollowsFormsBlocks followsBlockLine) fail for a different reason than the title says. Traced finish_application: the as-written call comparison itself fails (all five tries, abstracting included); the error shown is the earlier in-place lambda error (first_error), which is what suggested the ordering diagnosis. The goal comes from `match lower && isSome Colon second` / `rewrite deafOfStripped nextIndex …`, whose scrutinee/rule is hidden inside a folded call (rowStart, blockLine), so the usual (unfolded) search runs and the arm's goal is fully unfolded: Follows, Mark.Alike and runFrom gone, runPure already run against `state`. There `?j e` meets a continuation specialised to `state.at`, and `state` occurs outside the needle (later peeks read the same position), so the abstracting fallback rightly refuses. Experiment: the same proofs stated against the folded goal (the else branch as written; blockPeek … {modes | allow = nextIndex others}) check with no pair. So neither "hold the lambda" nor "compare on the call" can help; the fix is in how match/rewrite build the goal when the occurrence is inside a folded call (unfold only the calls on the path to it), a goal-as-written design question. Stopped for that.

- Check times (elab/kernel ms, --no-cache, same binary, load ~7-12): Statements 3673/529 -> 3767/572; DeclData 10732/200 -> 9925/185; DeclHeaders 729/134 -> 768/141 (noise). Moved to review: decision needed on the match/rewrite goal shape for the last 2.

[Opus] SW-4359 N1: f.induct takes its IH from eqK's right side (now sound guard) while the split binds the arm's own h; a recursive call whose argument computes with an && guard's proof at a non-skipped position could make the kernel refuse f.induct. tickets.body:
Estimate 35 min (lane started 10:10).
10:20 No reproducer. The exact N1 shape (a recursive argument that computes with the guard's proof, `pick x y` doing `match ok | Both _ _ => x`) gets no eqK at all, before and after SW-4344: the eqK walk requires the arm's whole branch to reach h only at positions conversion skips (`proof_is_inert_in`, D2180, since SW-1429), because a conjunction has no uniqueness lemma. Skipped positions stay skipped for any proof, so sound (complete h) converts with h. Checked with the current binary: a proof field (mkGap into the accumulator), an inert parameter in an inner `if`, an inner split over a constructor holding the proof, and a `decreasing` proof from the guard all get f.induct. Commit 407694be6 only adds that reasoning as a comment at the IH site in induct.rs.
10:22 Follow-up from the orchestrator: commit 50e761f7c adds examples/accept/and-guard-proof-in-induct.sw (collect, keep, climb, each with a proof by its f.induct) and its hash snapshot. test:example and test:lane AREA=hashes pass.

tickets.body:
Lane notes (Opus, 20 Nov 15:37-15:43): STOPPED before implementing, scope (D3688). No commits.

`byWalking` is a Lower token, unlike `cases` (KwCases). Today the self-hosted parser reads `byWalking [x]` at the start of an expression as App (Atom byWalking) [List], and slice 1 accepts it: `inGrammar1 "def a: T := byWalking [x]\n"` is True today (grammar1 takes App of names and lists). Rust reads it as a Walk (checked with `stitchwort dev tree --print`). The same holds for `(byWalking [x, y])`, `[byWalking [x]]`, and for 6a `if byWalking [x] then a else b`, which Rust refuses as an Error node and the self-hosted parser accepts as an If.

Effects of a parser case that matches Rust:
1. Narrowing (D3688): those sources leave inGrammar1 and the slices, so the proved formatter refuses them. No statement text changes, but formatAccepts1 then covers fewer sources. This corrects a parser divergence from the language. It is still Matt's call.
2. New invariant: the read-back proofs (runsExprInline / InlinePlain in ReadBackRuns.sw, ReadBackEnds.sw, ReadBackTree.sw; readsExprInline in ParseCarriesLadder.sw) would need a `noWalk` look-ahead fact. For within1..within6a trees, that needs a new tree invariant: no App with head Atom "byWalking" and a list as its first argument at an expression start. Otherwise parse(print t) = t is false for such a tree. This is more than the Cases pattern, so the brief says stop.
The mechanical part (Expr form, traversals, printer, Follows twin, the Gives proof for walkExpr, an Outside field) is as the brief says and was not started.

Orchestrator, 20 Nov: parked on D3704 (scope): matching Rust makes slices 1-6a refuse byWalking [ at an expression start unless Walk enters the slices. Lane report summary kept in the ticket notes above.

D3704 (Matt, 20 Nov 2026): yes, walks join the slices; no source accepted today is refused. "as we add new constructs to Stitchwort, we should also update the Stitchwort formatter. I guess it depends whether or not the construct goes in the slice that we have now or not. But yes, I think we should keep both in sync to the degree that makes sense at that stage." Next lane: Opus, Walk form + read-back invariant (byWalking [ at an expression start is a walk), the then form included; Fable checks the statements after.

Matt, 20 Nov 2026: "If byWalking falls within slice one's grammar today, then we should fix that. We should make it supported." Keep the slice 1 proofs updated.


Lane notes (Opus, 20 Nov 16:08-16:15): STOPPED before implementing, brief item 4 (narrowing, D3688). No commits.

Matching Rust's parser refuses sources that inGrammar1 accepts today. Checked by byComputing on this branch (all True today: inGrammar1, and formatWithin1 accepts them) and with the Rust formatter (each is [E-PARSE]):
- def a: T := byWalking [x] y          (Rust: expected the end of the declaration, but found y)
- def a: T := byWalking [x] + 1        (found +)
- def a: T := byWalking [x] -> B       (found ->)
- def a: T := byWalking [x] == byWalking [y]   (found ==)
- def a: T := byWalking [x] && y       (found &&)
- def a: T := (byWalking [x] y, 1)     (inGrammar1 True; same class inside a tuple)
The class: at an expression start (a def's type or value, after ( or [ or a comma, right of ->), byWalking [ ... ] followed by more of an expression (call arguments, a binary operator, an arrow). Rust's walk_expr returns right after the list (or the then body), so whatever follows is an error; the self-hosted parser reads a call. Plain walks (def a: T := byWalking [x], (byWalking [x, y]), [byWalking [x]], def b: byWalking [x] := b) stay in. Positions that are no expression start stay calls in both parsers (f byWalking [x], a + byWalking [x], -byWalking [x], A -> byWalking [x] is a walk: right of -> is an expression start). byWalking[x] with no space is also a walk.

inGrammar1 is defined through parseFile, so the parser change alone removes the class from slice 1's grammar without editing Grammar1.sw; formatAccepts1's statement is unchanged but covers fewer sources. MustAccept1 has no byWalking case.

Scale, for the plan: plain walks entering within1 (Slice1.sw, a frozen Scope definition) means every gated slice 1 lemma that splits on forms gains a Walk arm with content: shaped/lexical/settled facts, rule N, P2, elements and hangs, spelling, calm, meaning, read-back (exprOther's new walk branch; InlinePlain and runsExprInline gain a noWalk fact, which needs a tree invariant: no App with head Atom byWalking and a list first argument at an expression start). For a gauge, Prefix has 184 match arms across tools/fmt/src. Estimate: several Opus lanes, not 120 min.

D3705 (Matt, 20 Nov 2026): yes, the self-hosted parser matches Rust; sources Rust refuses (byWalking [x] y, + 1, -> B, ==, &&, inside a tuple) leave slice 1. "if the Rust parser doesn't accept some forms, the Stitchwork parser shouldn't either ... make them in sync." Which slice walks belong to: asked as D3706.

D3706 (Matt, 20 Nov 2026): yes. byWalking leaves slice 1's grammar (it entered only by the parser misreading it as a call) and joins slice 6a with the other proof steps; proved when 6a is. Plan: one lane: Walk form + parser as Rust + traversals + printer as Rust in slice 6a's program; slice 1 proofs gain the tree fact that no byWalking-headed list call sits at an expression start; top theorem statements unchanged; Fable checks statements after.


Lane (Opus, 20 Nov 17:45): done, 3 commits on lane/SW-4427 (53bd028ac Walk form, parser as Rust, printer, 6a; c3719f2d5 Follows twin + Parse.Gives; a4c61cdc8 slice 1 narrowing + read-back). Way taken for step 2: the name byWalking is out of grammar1 and within1 everywhere (D3706 "altogether"), and autoPlaced gains the Atom arm, so read-back gets walkOn = False at an expression start from the tree (notWalkFirst/noWalkLine) and the parse side gets it from the grammar; a positional fact (no byWalking-list call at a full start) needed a modes-aware ladder fact on the parse side (the [ not stopped) and was dropped. Extra narrowing beyond the walk sources: byWalking as an operand or alone (x + byWalking [y], def a: byWalking := b, f byWalking) is out of slice 1 too; later slices still format it as Rust. tickets.body:
Lane note (Sonnet): (1) Cause found, no fix merged. Expected-type-first unification compares Pass (framed ?d) with Pass (el ..); same_arguments_solving_nothing refuses the argument solution, both are unfolded to Joins, and Joins (Group x _) reduces to Joins x while Joins ?d is stuck, so ?d := x (inner of the group), not Group x; the later proof argument then mismatches. Only Group-like wrappers that Joins reads through trigger it (Paren and App arms accept _). Tried: in same_calls, solve by whole-argument unknowns (unify_by_unknown_arguments) first when one call is blocked, with narrowings (same-def after force; unknown against a Ctor); both still broke std/Args/Args.sw (Args.helpListsOption: List.memAppendRight/Left holes need the unfolding). Reproducer: scratchpad sw4475/repro-hole-argument.sw. (2) W-REWRITE-REPEATEDLY-UNUSED is right: close_parts closes a conjunct by a hypothesis (or part of one), so a listed hypothesis used only that way is never applied as a rewrite and can be dropped. No change.


Result (Sonnet lane, 20 Nov): (2) the warning is right: rewrite repeatedly closes a conjunct by a hypothesis part via try_close, so a listed rule used only that way is never applied; no change. (1) cause found, not fixed: the expected type is unified before the later proof argument; Joins (Group x _) unfolds to Joins x and the unifier solves ?d := x (the contents), not Group x. Reproducer and the unfinished unifier patch (solve by whole-argument unknowns when one call is blocked; broke std Args.helpListsOption memAppend holes) in docs/reviews/SW-4475/. Follow-up filed.

tickets.title: [Opus] Search: 6775 of 7012 recorded proof uses fail their own lemma's filtered first pass, because a use pattern's constants include its arguments' constants, which the lemma's type doesn't name (SW-4579). Decide whether use patterns should leave the arguments' constants out of the filter (and what that does to recall@10 and out-of-budget in search_bench::proof_uses_find_their_lemma_among_the_first_ten), and do it if it helps
tickets.body:
Lane (Opus, 22 Nov, from 08:00; est. 45 min), branch lane/SW-4585:
- Baseline (all profile, 1007 s): 10347 queries, recall@10 55.4%, top-1 41.3%, 39110 out of budget; 3572 pass their own lemma's filter (so 6775 fail), 5520 answered by the filtered pass.
- Trying: written = the lemma's conclusion only (args left out), and written = conclusion plus only the args it mentions.

- Cause: use_pattern's Pattern::constants (the conclusion with the arguments put in) and its written set (the conclusion as stated plus every argument) both name the arguments' definitions; the filter wants a candidate naming all of one set, and the generic lemma a proof instantiates doesn't. The lemma is then found only when nothing else passes and the relaxed pass runs.
- stitchwort search builds queries the same way (search_pattern: folded constants plus constants of the whole written term), so a goal-shaped query loses a generic lemma in the filtered pass just as the bench's uses do; leaving the arguments out would let the bench know the answer's constants, which no user query does.
- Measured (all profile): conclusion only: recall@10 55.4 -> 54.6, not found 3236 -> 4211, top-1 41.3 -> 43.3, out of budget 39110 -> 25843: dropped. Conclusion plus only the arguments it mentions: recall@10 and top-1 unchanged, out of budget 39110 -> 38733, not found 3236 -> 3253: kept (commit 5ad583eeb), with the bench now printing own-filter passes and filtered-pass answers.
- Tests: search_bench::a_use_pattern_passes_its_own_lemmas_filter, proof_use_of_flipped_run_..., proof_use_with_lambda_arguments_... pass; clippy clean. Each bench run 10-17 min.
Model result: Opus, worked, 57 min (est. 45)

tickets.body: Progress (Opus, 24 Nov): audit table in docs/reviews/SW-4750-cancellation-audit.md. One cancellation bug fixed: a --recheck (or carried-over) namespace replay cancelled while its digest is computed again reported E-CACHE-DIGEST and blanked this build's entry; now a late miss (test check_cache::a_recheck_cancelled_while_its_digest_is_computed_keeps_the_entry, fails before). One running-out bug found, not fixed (spreads): trial/declhash hashes that run out read as None and two Nones are 'kept'. SW-4744's namespace test half was vacuous (fixture had an unknown name); fixed.

tickets.title: [Opus] D3736: a def or theorem written inside a theorem's (or instance's? decide by the rule: anything whose body is sealed) proof is private to that proof: naming it from outside is an error saying so; local defs in ordinary defs stay nameable (sumTo.go); interface digest treats them as proof-private like %match helpers; guide + syntax.md
tickets.body: Progress (Opus lane, 24 Nov): done in fe622f0a1. Repo search: no use outside its theorem's proof except examples/reject/opaque-note-local-definition-theorem.sw (already a reject example; removed). Owners: theorems only (Def::proof_hidden needs the theorem flag; a Prop-typed def or instance computes, so stays nameable); compiler-made equation theorems (f.eq2) are not owners. E-PROOF-PRIVATE in resolve/unknown, dot paths (f.go) and stitchwort axioms; digest leaves them, their names and helper keys out; equation_skips rows owned. Tests: check_cache::digest (39/39, 3 new), examples local/proof-local/opaque-note/function-equations, decreasing_twins local, hash_stability for the new accept example.
